The item is already precise in structure but its cutoff is mis-sourced and its evidence route is wrong. The cited claim_01M4YGKFS9V8MZAS1VB9ACXDYD states a range of approximately 380–500 Da as the range within which clinically relevant kinase inhibitors typically fall, described as close to the upper limit compatible with efficient passive diffusion. That is a reported range/heuristic, not a decision threshold, so cutoff_basis should be source_stated_value with a bound_support record whose statement_kind is provides_heuristic and whose interpretation is the_heuristic_is_the_line (the 500 Da edge is the upper limit of the reported range). The 610.5 Da value in claim_01M4YVYAWREWGQYJV645KF3WFT is a single compound's molecular weight, not a threshold, and claim_01M4YJSFSJVXWB8MSVFTAQ8YFW states no number at all, so neither supports a cutoff. The attribute should also use the deterministic PubChem computed descriptor route (property_estimate/computed_property, derived) rather than the ADMET model panel, since the catalog explicitly says to prefer the exact descriptor route for MolecularWeight; the model-prediction route is a surrogate and would make this a separate predicted attribute. Direction lower_better and preference rule kind are appropriate for a drug-likeness ranking.

attribute.definition: Reported absolute or relative oral bioavailability (F%) in humans, as a measured pharmacokinetic parameter. Higher values indicate greater fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation intact.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "oral bioavailability"

attribute.name: Oral bioavailability (human, measured F%)
attribute.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of an oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans. The objective requires oral administration; a measured human F% is the most decision-relevant absorption parameter. Multiple claims report human F% values (e.g., 58%, 38-49%, 85-90%, 21.4%, 4.7%, 69-83%, 25%).

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower values; candidates with F% >= 20% receive a preference boost.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with F% < 20% is approved and clinically effective as an oral agent for the required targets, the threshold is too stringent.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim reports a measured human oral bioavailability of 21.4% for a drug that is orally administered and clinically used. This value is a real-world example of an acceptable human F% for an oral kinase inhibitor, supporting a preference threshold at or above 20%.

interpretation.measurement: The passage reports a measured human oral bioavailability of 21.4%.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidate set consists of orally administered kinase inhibitors intended for clinical development. A human F% of at least 20% is a reasonable lower bound for adequate systemic exposure, as exemplified by this measured value for an approved oral drug.

validator_problems: bound_support_mismatch: the support record for rule.cutoff.value states 21.4 % and its declared identity produces 21.4, while the executable parameter is 20 %

attribute.definition: Molecular weight of the compound in Daltons, as computed from structure. Lower values are generally associated with better oral absorption.

attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a key physicochemical determinant of oral absorption. Claims state that most clinically relevant kinase inhibitors fall within 380-500 Da and that drugs with MW < 500 Da have acceptable oral bioavailability. The Lipinski rule of 5 uses MW < 500 Da as a criterion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with MW <= 500 Da above those with higher MW; candidates with MW > 500 Da are penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with MW > 500 Da is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the threshold is too strict.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim explicitly states that drugs with MW < 500 Da have acceptable oral bioavailability, making this a decision threshold for oral absorption.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of oral bioavailability from the ADMET-AI model (Bioavailability_Ma). Higher probability indicates better oral bioavailability.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al.)
attribute.rationale: Directly predicts oral bioavailability. The model has moderate held-out AUPRC (0.87) and AUROC (0.7164).

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with oral bioavailability probability >= 0.5 above those with lower probability.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with oral bioavailability probability < 0.5 is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the threshold is too strict.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L). Higher values indicate better solubility, which can enhance oral absorption.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Aqueous solubility is a prerequisite for oral absorption. The model has good held-out R² (0.8166) and MAE (0.6921).

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted solubility above those with lower solubility.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with solubility < -5 log(mol/L) is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the threshold is too strict.

attribute.definition: Predicted Caco-2 cell effective permeability. Higher values indicate better intestinal permeability.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)
attribute.rationale: Caco-2 permeability is a standard in vitro measure of intestinal permeability. The model has moderate held-out R² (0.7065) and MAE (0.3115).

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher Caco-2 permeability above those with lower permeability.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with Caco-2 permeability < -6 is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the threshold is too strict.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of P-glycoprotein inhibition. Lower probability is preferred to avoid efflux-mediated reduction in oral absorption.
attribute.name: P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-glycoprotein efflux limits oral absorption. The claim states that overexpression of efflux transporters such as P-gp limits intracellular drug accumulation. The model has high held-out AUPRC (0.9581) and AUROC (0.9475).

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower P-gp inhibition probability above those with higher probability.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with high P-gp inhibition probability is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the threshold is too strict.

attribute.definition: Time to reach maximum plasma concentration after oral administration, in hours. Shorter times indicate faster absorption.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "Tmax"

attribute.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax)
attribute.rationale: Tmax is a measure of the rate of oral absorption. Claims report Tmax values ranging from 1 to 12 hours for various oral drugs. Faster absorption (lower Tmax) is generally preferred for oral drugs.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with Tmax <= 4 h above those with longer Tmax.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with Tmax > 4 h is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the threshold is too strict.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim reports a measured Tmax of about 4 h for an orally administered drug, indicating rapid absorption. This value is a real-world example of acceptable Tmax for an oral kinase inhibitor.

interpretation.measurement: The passage reports a measured Tmax of about 4 h.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidate set consists of orally administered kinase inhibitors. A Tmax of 4 h or less is a reasonable upper bound for rapid absorption, as exemplified by this measured value.

attribute.definition: Whether oral absorption is significantly affected by food intake. Absence of a clinically relevant food effect is preferred for consistent dosing.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "food effect"

attribute.name: Food effect on absorption (qualitative)
attribute.rationale: Food effects can alter oral bioavailability and complicate dosing. Claims mention that food intake affects bioavailability for some drugs, while others have no relevant food effect.

payload.expected_change: Preserves information about food effects for consideration; candidates with no food effect may be preferred.
payload.falsification_test: If food effect data is unavailable for most candidates, this criterion will not discriminate.
validator_problems: schema: literature evidence yields numbers with units; a literature-bound attribute must be quantitative with a unit

attribute.definition: Whether the compound is documented as orally administered in humans (e.g., approved oral drug, clinical trial oral dosing).
attribute.name: Oral administration route (recorded)
attribute.rationale: The task requires oral administration. This attribute records whether the compound has a documented oral route in humans, which is a prerequisite for the objective.

payload.expected_change: Excludes candidates without documented oral administration; only candidates with oral=true proceed.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate without a documented oral route is later found to be orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the exclusion is too strict.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim states that nearly all TKIs are effective when taken orally, and the task explicitly requires oral administration. A documented oral route is a requirement for the objective.

validator_problems: schema: a support record names parameter 'rule.cutoff.value', which this criterion does not hold; a record supporting nothing would read as support for everything

attribute.definition: Absolute oral bioavailability (F%) measured in humans, as reported in peer-reviewed literature or regulatory reviews. Higher values indicate a larger fraction of the oral dose reaching systemic circulation.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("oral bioavailability" OR "absolute bioavailability" OR "F%") AND (human OR clinical)

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
attribute.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of an oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans, the most clinically relevant absorption parameter. The task requires oral administration; a measured human F% is the gold-standard evidence for oral bioavailability. Claims claim_01M4XQ3T71E23Q3NW5CRHRNT2H (4.7%) and claim_01M4XQ6215HEFM6TRKGCYH5AQA (98%) show that human F% values are reported and span a wide range, supporting a preference ranking. No source-stated cutoff for a minimum acceptable F% is present in the claims, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower values, favouring compounds with better absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with low measured human F% (e.g., <10%) is clinically effective orally at tolerated doses, the preference for high F% would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of oral bioavailability from the ADMET-AI model (Bioavailability_Ma endpoint), a classifier's probability of its positive class in [0,1]. Higher values indicate a higher likelihood of oral bioavailability.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al.)
attribute.rationale: Provides a model-predicted probability of oral bioavailability for every compound with a structure, covering the whole library where measured human F% is sparse. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.7164, so it is a moderate-quality predictor; used as a preference, not a hard exclusion. No source-stated cutoff exists for this model output, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted oral bioavailability probability above those with lower values, providing a continuous score for all compounds.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted probability (<0.3) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the model's utility as a preference would be questioned.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of human intestinal absorption from the ADMET-AI model (HIA_Hou endpoint), a classifier's probability of its positive class in [0,1]. Higher values indicate a higher likelihood of intestinal absorption.
attribute.name: Human intestinal absorption (HIA) probability
attribute.rationale: Intestinal absorption is a prerequisite for oral bioavailability. The HIA_Hou model has high held-out AUROC (0.994), making it a strong predictor. Used as a preference to rank candidates by predicted absorption. No source-stated cutoff exists for this model output, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted HIA probability above those with lower values, favouring compounds likely to be absorbed.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted HIA probability (<0.5) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the model's utility as a preference would be questioned.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility from the ADMET-AI model (Solubility_AqSolDB endpoint) in log(mol/L). Higher values indicate greater solubility.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Aqueous solubility is required for dissolution in gastrointestinal fluid, a prerequisite for oral absorption (claim_01M4XQ61HGKAPDSK6ZNDWZT8DB). The model has held-out R2 0.8166, a good regression predictor. Used as a preference to rank candidates by predicted solubility. No source-stated cutoff exists for this model output, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted aqueous solubility above those with lower values, favouring compounds that can dissolve for absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted solubility (< -6 log mol/L) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the model's utility as a preference would be questioned.

attribute.definition: Predicted cell effective permeability from the ADMET-AI model (Caco2_Wang endpoint) in log(10^-6 cm/s). Higher values indicate greater permeability.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)
attribute.rationale: Intestinal permeability is a key determinant of oral absorption (claim_01M4XQ61HGKAPDSK6ZNDWZT8DB). The Caco2_Wang model has held-out R2 0.7065, a moderate regression predictor. Used as a preference to rank candidates by predicted permeability. No source-stated cutoff exists for this model output, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted Caco-2 permeability above those with lower values, favouring compounds likely to cross the intestinal epithelium.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted Caco-2 permeability (< -6 log 10^-6 cm/s) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the model's utility as a preference would be questioned.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of P-glycoprotein inhibition from the ADMET-AI model (Pgp_Broccatelli endpoint) in [0,1]. Higher values indicate a higher likelihood of P-gp inhibition, which may reduce oral absorption of co-administered drugs but is not directly a property of the candidate's own absorption.
attribute.name: P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-glycoprotein efflux can limit oral absorption (claim_01M4XQ61HGKAPDSK6ZNDWZT8DB). The model has held-out AUROC 0.9475, a strong classifier. Used as a preference to rank candidates with lower predicted P-gp inhibition higher, as this may correlate with better absorption. No source-stated cutoff exists for this model output, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower predicted P-gp inhibition probability above those with higher values, favouring compounds less likely to be effluxed.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high predicted P-gp inhibition probability (>0.8) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the model's utility as a preference would be questioned.

attribute.definition: Molecular weight in Daltons, computed from the structure. Lower values are generally associated with better passive diffusion and oral absorption.
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)
attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a critical determinant of passive diffusion and oral bioavailability (claim_01M4YGKFRNK9FK4DPA82VEY582, claim_01M4YGKFSSCZC9WWXP1BXD8D41). Most clinically relevant kinase inhibitors fall within 380–500 Da (claim_01M4YGKFS9V8MZAS1VB9ACXDYD). Used as a preference to rank candidates with lower molecular weight higher. No source-stated cutoff for a maximum acceptable MW is present, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower molecular weight above those with higher values, favouring compounds with better passive diffusion.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high molecular weight (>500 Da) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for lower MW would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Lipophilicity (logP) computed from the structure. Moderate lipophilicity (logP ≈ 2–4) is considered optimal for kinase inhibitors.
attribute.name: Lipophilicity (logP)
attribute.rationale: Moderate lipophilicity (logP ≈ 2–4) is considered optimal for kinase inhibitors (claim_01M4YGKFT8T97H08A3RS5A2H24). Excessive lipophilicity leads to poor solubility and increased metabolic clearance (claim_01M4YGKFTX7A37M77HHQX99A1P). Used as a preference to rank candidates closer to the 2–4 range higher. No source-stated cutoff for a hard exclusion is present, so the rule ranks by distance from the range.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with logP closer to the 2–4 range above those outside it, favouring compounds with optimal lipophilicity for oral absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with logP outside 2–4 are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for the 2–4 range would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Topological polar surface area (TPSA) in Å², computed from the structure. Lower values are generally associated with better passive diffusion.
attribute.name: Topological polar surface area (TPSA)
attribute.rationale: Lower polarity (TPSA below approximately 90 Å²) is associated with enhanced passive diffusion (claim_01M4YGKFVFREF8CCARQHNQZJCY). Used as a preference to rank candidates with lower TPSA higher. No source-stated cutoff for a hard exclusion is present, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower TPSA above those with higher values, favouring compounds with better passive diffusion.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high TPSA (>90 Å²) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for lower TPSA would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Number of rotatable bonds, computed from the structure. Lower values indicate reduced molecular flexibility, which is generally associated with improved passive diffusion and oral bioavailability.
attribute.name: Rotatable bond count
attribute.rationale: Molecular flexibility, estimated by rotatable bonds, is a determinant of oral bioavailability and membrane permeability (claim_01M4YGKG0DJNW7V10MH51VPEVR). Reduced conformational flexibility improves passive diffusion (claim_01M4XPWAK6CGBR7K32B1PDYDTA). Used as a preference to rank candidates with fewer rotatable bonds higher. No source-stated cutoff for a hard exclusion is present, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with fewer rotatable bonds above those with more, favouring compounds with better passive diffusion.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high rotatable bond count (>10) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for fewer rotatable bonds would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Number of Lipinski rule of 5 violations, computed from the structure. Fewer violations indicate better drug-likeness and oral absorption potential.
attribute.name: Lipinski rule of 5 compliance (count of violations)
attribute.rationale: Lipinski rule of 5 is a widely used heuristic for oral drug-likeness. The ADMET-AI panel provides a computed count of violations. Used as a preference to rank candidates with fewer violations higher. No source-stated cutoff for a hard exclusion is present, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with fewer Lipinski violations above those with more, favouring compounds with better drug-likeness.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with multiple Lipinski violations (>2) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for fewer violations would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Recorded flag indicating whether the compound is administered orally, from the ChEMBL molecule record. A true value indicates documented oral administration.
attribute.name: Oral administration route (recorded)
attribute.rationale: The task requires oral administration. A recorded oral flag provides direct evidence that the compound is administered orally. Used as a preference to rank candidates with a recorded oral flag higher. No source-stated cutoff exists for this categorical field, so the rule ranks by presence of the flag.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with a recorded oral administration flag above those without, favouring compounds known to be orally administered.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate without a recorded oral flag is found to be orally administered in humans, the preference for the flag would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Qualitative assessment of whether food intake substantially alters oral absorption, as reported in the literature. Compounds with minimal food effect are preferred for predictable dosing.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("food effect" OR "food intake" OR "fed" OR "fasted") AND (absorption OR bioavailability)

attribute.name: Food effect on absorption (qualitative)
attribute.rationale: Food can alter bioavailability several-fold (claim_01M4XQ61JPCAFF0FQ7J2MTNBCW), and examples show large effects (claim_01M4XQ61MC226CZM3G14KMDA4K, claim_01M4XQ61MYH3JCVH9WGWQN421H). A compound with minimal food effect is preferred for predictable oral dosing. Used as an exploratory consideration to record the qualitative assessment without a preference score. No source-stated cutoff exists, so the rule records the observation.

payload.expected_change: Records whether a substantial food effect on absorption is reported, allowing later stages to consider it without affecting ranking.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with a large food effect is found to have consistent oral bioavailability across fed and fasted states, the concern would be reduced.
validator_problems: schema: literature evidence yields numbers with units; a literature-bound attribute must be quantitative with a unit

attribute.definition: Time to reach maximum plasma concentration (Tmax) after oral administration, in hours, as reported in the literature. Shorter Tmax indicates faster absorption.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("Tmax" OR "time to maximum concentration" OR "peak plasma") AND (oral OR pharmacokinetics)

attribute.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax)
attribute.rationale: Tmax is a standard pharmacokinetic parameter reflecting the rate of oral absorption. Faster absorption (shorter Tmax) is generally preferred for oral drugs. Used as a preference to rank candidates with shorter Tmax higher. No source-stated cutoff exists, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with shorter Tmax above those with longer Tmax, favouring faster oral absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with long Tmax (>6 h) is found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for shorter Tmax would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Absolute or relative oral bioavailability measured in humans, expressed as percent of administered dose reaching systemic circulation. Values are pooled across sources reporting a human F% for the compound.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "oral bioavailability"

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
attribute.rationale: The task requires oral administration; measured human F% is the most direct evidence of adequate oral absorption. Claim_01M4YGXW3G7712TV7ZPB5Y5F9A reports 4.7% absolute bioavailability for a compound, providing a source-stated value that can serve as a lower bound for screening.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with measured human oral bioavailability at or above 4.7% higher; compounds with lower or unknown F% rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with F% < 4.7% is later shown to achieve adequate systemic exposure and target engagement in humans, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of human intestinal absorption from the ADMET-AI model (HIA_Hou endpoint), a classifier's probability of its positive class in [0,1].
attribute.name: Human intestinal absorption (HIA) probability
attribute.rationale: HIA probability is a model-predicted surrogate for oral absorption, computable for every compound with a structure. It is an auxiliary preference, not a hard exclusion, because it is a prediction.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with predicted HIA probability >= 0.5 higher; compounds below 0.5 rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with HIA probability < 0.5 is shown to have adequate oral absorption in humans, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of oral bioavailability from the ADMET-AI model (Bioavailability_Ma endpoint), a classifier's probability of its positive class in [0,1].
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al.)
attribute.rationale: Bioavailability_Ma is a model-predicted probability of oral bioavailability, computable for every compound with a structure. It is an auxiliary preference, not a hard exclusion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with predicted oral bioavailability probability >= 0.5 higher; compounds below 0.5 rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with Bioavailability_Ma probability < 0.5 is shown to have adequate oral bioavailability in humans, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility from the ADMET-AI model (Solubility_AqSolDB endpoint), a regression value in log(mol/L). Higher values indicate greater solubility.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Aqueous solubility is a key determinant of oral absorption. The model provides a predicted value for every compound with a structure. It is an auxiliary preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with predicted aqueous solubility >= -6 log(mol/L) higher; compounds below rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with predicted solubility < -6 log(mol/L) is shown to have adequate oral absorption, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted cell effective permeability from the ADMET-AI model (Caco2_Wang endpoint), a regression value in log(10^-6 cm/s). Higher values indicate greater permeability.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)
attribute.rationale: Caco-2 permeability is a model-predicted surrogate for intestinal permeability, computable for every compound with a structure. It is an auxiliary preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with predicted Caco-2 permeability >= -6 log(10^-6 cm/s) higher; compounds below rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with predicted Caco-2 permeability < -6 log(10^-6 cm/s) is shown to have adequate oral absorption, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of P-glycoprotein inhibition from the ADMET-AI model (Pgp_Broccatelli endpoint), a classifier's probability of its positive class in [0,1]. Higher values indicate greater likelihood of P-gp inhibition, which may limit oral absorption.
attribute.name: P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-gp inhibition can reduce oral bioavailability by increasing efflux. The model provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. It is an auxiliary preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with predicted P-gp inhibition probability <= 0.5 higher; compounds above 0.5 rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with P-gp inhibition probability > 0.5 is shown to have adequate oral absorption, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Computed molecular weight from PubChem (property_estimate / computed_property), in g/mol. Lower values are generally favorable for oral absorption.
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)
attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a fundamental physicochemical property influencing oral absorption. The PubChem computed descriptor is a derived value, not a measurement.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with molecular weight <= 500 g/mol higher; compounds above rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with molecular weight > 500 g/mol is shown to have adequate oral absorption, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Computed XLogP from PubChem (property_estimate / computed_property), in log units. Values within a moderate range are favorable for oral absorption.
attribute.name: Lipophilicity (logP)
attribute.rationale: Lipophilicity is a key determinant of membrane permeability and solubility. The PubChem computed descriptor is a derived value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with logP >= -0.4 higher; compounds below rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with logP < -0.4 is shown to have adequate oral absorption, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Computed TPSA from PubChem (property_estimate / computed_property), in Å². Lower values are generally favorable for oral absorption.
attribute.name: Topological polar surface area (TPSA)
attribute.rationale: TPSA is a predictor of passive membrane permeability. The PubChem computed descriptor is a derived value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with TPSA <= 140 Å² higher; compounds above rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with TPSA > 140 Å² is shown to have adequate oral absorption, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: Number of Lipinski rule-of-five violations, computed from the structure (predicted_property_lookup / Lipinski endpoint). Lower counts are favorable for oral absorption.
attribute.name: Lipinski rule of 5 compliance (count of violations)
attribute.rationale: Lipinski rule-of-five violations are a standard heuristic for oral drug-likeness. The endpoint is computed by RDKit, not a trained model, but is reported under the predicted route.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with <= 1 Lipinski violation higher; compounds with more violations rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with > 1 Lipinski violation is shown to have adequate oral absorption, the cutoff is falsified.

attribute.definition: ChEMBL molecule record field 'oral' indicating whether the compound is documented as orally administered. Categorical boolean.
attribute.name: Oral administration route (recorded)
attribute.rationale: The task requires oral administration. The ChEMBL record field 'oral' provides a curated boolean indicating whether the compound is documented as orally administered. This is a direct requirement, but the field is often empty before approval, so absence gives unknown, never fail.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with a recorded oral administration flag higher; compounds without the flag rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound without a recorded oral flag is shown to be orally administered, the preference is falsified.

attribute.definition: Qualitative assessment of whether food intake significantly affects oral absorption, based on literature reports. Compounds with no relevant food effect are preferred.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "food effect" AND "absorption"

attribute.name: Food effect on absorption (qualitative)
attribute.rationale: Food effects can alter oral bioavailability and complicate dosing. Claims such as claim_01M4YGXW5CAC9A8HKXKFME7G8H report a 20% exposure increase with food for a compound, indicating a food effect. This is a qualitative consideration.

payload.expected_change: Preserves food effect information for consideration; does not rank or exclude.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with a reported food effect is shown to have no clinically significant impact on exposure, the consideration is weakened.
validator_problems: schema: literature evidence yields numbers with units; a literature-bound attribute must be quantitative with a unit

attribute.definition: Time to reach peak plasma concentration after oral administration, in hours. Shorter Tmax may indicate faster absorption.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "Tmax" AND "oral"

attribute.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax)
attribute.rationale: Tmax is a pharmacokinetic parameter reflecting absorption rate. Claim_01M4YGXW4A4JEC03DM07BZ710Z reports Tmax of 2-4 hours for a compound. This is an exploratory consideration.

payload.expected_change: Preserves Tmax information for consideration; does not rank or exclude.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with a long Tmax is shown to have adequate oral absorption, the consideration is weakened.

attribute.definition: Fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation unchanged in humans, as reported in peer-reviewed literature. Higher values indicate better oral absorption and first-pass survival.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "oral bioavailability" AND (human OR clinical)

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
attribute.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans, the most clinically relevant absorption parameter. The task requires oral administration; a compound with negligible human F% cannot achieve adequate systemic exposure for tumour-microenvironment target engagement.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower or unknown values, favouring compounds with demonstrated clinical absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with low or unknown human F% achieves comparable target engagement and clinical efficacy to one with high F%, the preference is not decision-relevant.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the TDC Bioavailability_Ma classifier (AUROC 0.7164). A model prediction, not a measurement.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al. model)
attribute.rationale: Provides a computed oral bioavailability probability for every compound with a structure, covering candidates lacking measured human F%. The model's AUROC of 0.7164 is modest but sufficient for a preference ranking, not a hard exclusion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted oral bioavailability probability above those with lower values, extending absorption assessment to compounds without measured human data.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted probabilities do not correlate with measured human F% in this compound set, the preference adds noise rather than signal.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of human intestinal absorption from the TDC HIA_Hou classifier (AUROC 0.994). A model prediction of the absorption step, not systemic bioavailability.
attribute.name: Human intestinal absorption (HIA) probability
attribute.rationale: High-accuracy model (AUROC 0.994) for the intestinal absorption step. A compound with low HIA probability is unlikely to be orally absorbed, though it may still have high F% if first-pass metabolism is minimal. Useful as a preference to flag absorption-limited candidates.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted HIA probability above those with lower values, favouring compounds likely to cross the intestinal epithelium.
payload.falsification_test: If candidates with low HIA probability still achieve adequate systemic exposure via oral dosing, the preference is not decision-relevant.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility from the TDC Solubility_AqSolDB regression model (R² 0.8166). Higher values indicate greater solubility, which supports dissolution and absorption after oral dosing.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Solubility is a prerequisite for oral absorption. The model has good regression performance (R² 0.8166). Low solubility can limit absorption even for permeable compounds. A preference, not a hard exclusion, because formulation can mitigate poor solubility.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted aqueous solubility above those with lower values, favouring compounds that can dissolve in the gastrointestinal tract.
payload.falsification_test: If poorly soluble candidates achieve adequate oral absorption through formulation or high permeability, the preference is not decision-relevant.

attribute.definition: Predicted effective permeability across Caco-2 cell monolayers from the TDC Caco2_Wang regression model (R² 0.7065). Higher values indicate greater intestinal permeability.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)
attribute.rationale: Caco-2 permeability is a standard in vitro surrogate for intestinal absorption. The model's R² of 0.7065 is moderate. Useful as a preference to rank candidates by likely absorption efficiency.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted Caco-2 permeability above those with lower values, favouring compounds likely to cross the intestinal barrier.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted Caco-2 permeability does not correlate with measured human absorption for this compound set, the preference adds noise.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound inhibits P-glycoprotein, from the TDC Pgp_Broccatelli classifier (AUROC 0.9475). High P-gp inhibition can limit oral absorption of co-administered drugs and may indicate transporter interaction.
attribute.name: P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-gp inhibition can affect drug-drug interactions and may reflect transporter affinity that limits absorption. Lower probability is preferred. A preference, not a hard exclusion, because P-gp inhibition is not directly disqualifying for oral absorption of the compound itself.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower predicted P-gp inhibition probability above those with higher values, favouring compounds less likely to have transporter-mediated absorption limitations or interaction liabilities.
payload.falsification_test: If P-gp inhibition probability does not correlate with oral absorption or drug-drug interaction risk in this set, the preference is not decision-relevant.

attribute.definition: Computed molecular weight from PubChem (derived descriptor). Lower molecular weight generally favours oral absorption; the Lipinski rule of 5 uses 500 Da as a threshold.
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)
attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a fundamental determinant of passive permeability and is part of the Lipinski rule of 5. Lower values are preferred for oral absorption. A preference, not a hard exclusion, because some large compounds are still orally bioavailable.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower molecular weight above those with higher values, favouring compounds more likely to be orally absorbed.

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
attribute.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of an oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans, the most clinically relevant absorption parameter. The task requires oral administration; a measured human F% is the gold-standard evidence for that requirement. No numeric cutoff is stated in the cited claims, so the rule ranks candidates by the value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower or unknown values; compounds with no human F% data receive no penalty but are not preferred.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with low measured human F% (<10%) is consistently ranked above candidates with high F% (>50%) by the overall workflow, this preference is not contributing as intended.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound is absorbed from the human gastrointestinal tract, from the ADMET-AI HIA_Hou classifier. Higher probability indicates greater likelihood of intestinal absorption.
attribute.name: Human intestinal absorption (HIA) probability
attribute.rationale: Intestinal absorption is a prerequisite for oral bioavailability. The model is computable for every compound with a structure, so it scores the whole universe. The natural decision boundary of a binary classifier is 0.5, but no cited claim states a numeric cutoff, so the rule ranks by probability.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted HIA probability above those with lower probability; compounds without a structure receive unknown and no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted HIA probability does not correlate with measured human F% in compounds where both are available, this preference is not informative.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the ADMET-AI Bioavailability_Ma classifier. Higher probability indicates greater likelihood of oral bioavailability.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al. model)
attribute.rationale: Directly predicts the probability of oral bioavailability, the key property for the oral route requirement. The model is computable for every compound with a structure. No cited claim states a numeric cutoff, so the rule ranks by probability.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted oral bioavailability probability above those with lower probability; compounds without a structure receive unknown and no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted oral bioavailability probability does not correlate with measured human F% in compounds where both are available, this preference is not informative.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB regression model. Higher values indicate greater solubility, which supports dissolution and absorption after oral dosing.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Aqueous solubility is a key determinant of oral absorption; poorly soluble compounds often show low and variable bioavailability. The model is computable for every compound with a structure. No cited claim states a numeric cutoff, so the rule ranks by solubility.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted aqueous solubility above those with lower solubility; compounds without a structure receive unknown and no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted aqueous solubility does not correlate with measured human F% in compounds where both are available, this preference is not informative.

attribute.definition: Predicted cell effective permeability in log(10^-6 cm/s) from the ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang regression model. Higher values indicate greater intestinal permeability.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted Caco-2 permeability above those with lower permeability; compounds without a structure receive unknown and no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted Caco-2 permeability does not correlate with measured human F% in compounds where both are available, this preference is not informative.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower predicted P-gp inhibition probability above those with higher probability; compounds without a structure receive unknown and no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted P-gp inhibition probability does not correlate with measured human F% in compounds where both are available, this preference is not informative.

attribute.definition: Computed molecular weight in g/mol from the compound's structure. Lower molecular weight is generally associated with better oral absorption.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower molecular weight above those with higher molecular weight; compounds without a structure receive unknown and no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If molecular weight does not correlate with measured human F% in compounds where both are available, this preference is not informative.

attribute.definition: Computed XLogP in log units from the compound's structure. Moderate lipophilicity is generally optimal for oral absorption; extreme values are unfavorable.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower TPSA above those with higher TPSA; compounds without a structure receive unknown and no penalty.

attribute.name: Human intestinal absorption (HIA) probability
attribute.rationale: Intestinal absorption is a prerequisite for oral bioavailability. The HIA_Hou model has high held-out AUROC (0.994), making it a reliable auxiliary preference. It is computable for any compound with a structure, so it scores the whole library. A preference ranks higher probabilities above lower ones; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted HIA probability above those with lower probability; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with high predicted HIA probability is experimentally shown to have negligible intestinal absorption, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound is orally bioavailable in humans, from the ADMET-AI Bioavailability_Ma classifier. Higher probability indicates greater likelihood of oral bioavailability.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al. model)
attribute.rationale: This model directly predicts oral bioavailability, the dimension of interest. Its held-out AUROC is 0.7164, moderate but informative. It is an auxiliary preference, not a hard exclusion. No source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted oral bioavailability probability above those with lower probability; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with high predicted oral bioavailability probability is experimentally shown to have negligible oral bioavailability, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model. Higher values indicate greater solubility, which supports dissolution and absorption.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Aqueous solubility is a key determinant of oral absorption. The model has held-out R2 0.8166, a good regression. It is an auxiliary preference; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted aqueous solubility above those with lower solubility; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with high predicted solubility is experimentally shown to have poor dissolution and absorption, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted cell effective permeability in log(10^-6 cm/s) from the ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang model. Higher values indicate greater permeability across intestinal epithelium.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)
attribute.rationale: Caco-2 permeability is a standard in vitro surrogate for intestinal permeability. The model has held-out R2 0.7065, moderate. It is an auxiliary preference; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted Caco-2 permeability above those with lower permeability; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with high predicted Caco-2 permeability is experimentally shown to have poor intestinal permeability, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound inhibits P-glycoprotein, from the ADMET-AI Pgp_Broccatelli classifier. Higher probability indicates greater likelihood of P-gp inhibition, which may limit oral absorption and distribution.
attribute.name: P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-gp efflux can reduce oral bioavailability. The model has high held-out AUROC (0.9475). Lower probability is preferred. It is an auxiliary preference; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted P-gp inhibition probability above those with higher probability; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with high predicted P-gp inhibition probability is experimentally shown to have high oral bioavailability, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Computed molecular weight in g/mol from PubChem. Lower molecular weight is generally favorable for oral absorption.
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)
attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a fundamental physicochemical property influencing oral absorption. The PubChem computed descriptor is a derived value. It is a preference; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower molecular weight above those with higher molecular weight; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with high molecular weight is experimentally shown to have excellent oral bioavailability, the preference's relevance is weakened.

attribute.definition: Computed XLogP in log units from PubChem. Moderate lipophilicity is generally favorable for oral absorption; extremely high or low values are unfavorable.
attribute.name: Lipophilicity (XLogP)
attribute.rationale: Lipophilicity affects membrane permeability and solubility. The PubChem computed descriptor is a derived value. It is a preference; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used. The direction is set to within_range to reflect that both extremes are unfavorable, but the rule uses ordering to rank by proximity to an optimal range (not specified in claims).

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with more favorable lipophilicity (closer to an optimal range) above those with extreme values; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with extreme lipophilicity is experimentally shown to have excellent oral bioavailability, the preference's relevance is weakened.

attribute.definition: Computed topological polar surface area in Å² from PubChem. Lower TPSA is generally favorable for oral absorption.
attribute.name: Topological polar surface area (TPSA)
attribute.rationale: TPSA is a key determinant of passive permeability. The PubChem computed descriptor is a derived value. It is a preference; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower TPSA above those with higher TPSA; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with high TPSA is experimentally shown to have excellent oral bioavailability, the preference's relevance is weakened.

attribute.definition: Number of Lipinski rule-of-5 violations computed by RDKit from the structure. Fewer violations indicate better drug-likeness and oral absorption potential.
attribute.name: Lipinski rule of 5 compliance (count of violations)
attribute.rationale: Lipinski violations are a standard heuristic for oral drug-likeness. The RDKit calculation is deterministic. It is a preference; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer Lipinski violations above those with more violations; compounds without a structure are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with multiple Lipinski violations is experimentally shown to have excellent oral bioavailability, the heuristic's relevance is weakened.

attribute.definition: Median time to peak plasma concentration after oral dosing, in hours, from peer-reviewed literature. Shorter Tmax indicates faster absorption.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "Tmax" AND (oral OR pharmacokinetics)

attribute.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax)
attribute.rationale: Tmax is a direct measure of absorption rate. Shorter Tmax is generally preferred for oral drugs. It is a preference; no source-stated cutoff exists, so ordering is used.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with shorter Tmax above those with longer Tmax; compounds with no measured Tmax are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with long Tmax is experimentally shown to have excellent oral bioavailability, the preference's relevance is weakened.

attribute.definition: Qualitative assessment of whether food intake significantly alters the extent or rate of oral absorption, from peer-reviewed literature. Absence of a food effect is preferred.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "food effect" AND (oral OR absorption)

attribute.name: Food effect on absorption (qualitative)
attribute.rationale: Food effects can complicate dosing and reduce bioavailability. This is an exploratory consideration to preserve qualitative evidence without imposing a preference score.

payload.expected_change: Records food effect information for each compound; does not rank or exclude.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with a reported food effect is later shown to have no clinically significant food effect, the recorded observation is updated.
validator_problems: schema: literature evidence yields numbers with units; a literature-bound attribute must be quantitative with a unit

attribute.definition: Model-predicted drug clearance from human hepatocytes, in uL/min/10^6 cells, used as a surrogate for hepatic metabolic stability. Lower values indicate slower metabolism and greater metabolic stability.
attribute.name: Predicted human liver microsomal intrinsic clearance (Clearance_Hepatocyte_AZ)
attribute.rationale: Metabolic stability is a stated requirement for drug-like properties (claim_01M4X8J2DN55T0X4HQ5F438MP8) and is a key determinant of oral exposure. The ADMET-AI model provides a predicted clearance value for every compound with a structure, enabling ranking across the library. The model's held-out R2 is 0.264, so this is an auxiliary preference, not a hard exclusion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by predicted hepatic clearance; compounds with lower predicted clearance are preferred, improving the likelihood of adequate oral exposure.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted clearance does not correlate with measured metabolic stability or oral exposure in a validation set, the preference should be discarded.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted P-gp inhibition higher; compounds above 0.5 are deprioritized.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted P-gp inhibition does not correlate with drug-drug interactions or toxicity in chronic dosing, the preference is not useful.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted plasma protein binding rate (%); very high binding can limit free drug availability and potentially reduce efficacy, but also may reduce toxicity from free drug.
attribute.name: Predicted plasma protein binding rate (PPBR_AZ)
attribute.rationale: High plasma protein binding can reduce the free fraction available to engage targets, potentially requiring higher doses and increasing toxicity risk. The ADMET-AI PPBR_AZ model (R2 0.5889) provides a computable surrogate.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted plasma protein binding higher; compounds above 90% are deprioritized.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted plasma protein binding does not correlate with free drug exposure or toxicity in chronic dosing, the preference is not useful.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of blood-brain barrier penetration; for a peripheral tumour-microenvironment target, high BBB penetration may increase CNS toxicity risk, but for brain tumors it may be desirable. Here, as a safety consideration for chronic oral dosing, lower penetration is preferred to limit CNS exposure.
attribute.name: Predicted blood-brain barrier penetration probability (BBB_Martins)
attribute.rationale: For a chronic oral agent targeting the tumour microenvironment outside the CNS, high BBB penetration could lead to CNS side effects; a lower probability is preferred. The ADMET-AI BBB_Martins model (AUROC 0.9004) provides a computable surrogate.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted BBB penetration higher; compounds above 0.5 are deprioritized.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted BBB penetration does not correlate with CNS toxicity in chronic dosing, the preference is not useful.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted hepatocyte clearance higher; compounds above 50 are deprioritized.

attribute.rationale: QED is a widely used metric for drug-likeness; higher scores indicate more favorable properties.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher QED scores higher.
payload.falsification_test: If QED does not correlate with successful development, the criterion is not useful.

attribute.definition: Number of Lipinski rule of 5 violations from RDKit, indicating potential oral bioavailability issues.
attribute.name: Predicted Lipinski rule of 5 violation count
attribute.rationale: Lipinski violations are associated with poor oral absorption; RDKit calculation.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer Lipinski violations higher.
payload.falsification_test: If Lipinski violations do not predict oral bioavailability, the criterion is not useful.

attribute.definition: Molecular weight in g/mol from RDKit.
attribute.name: Predicted molecular weight
attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a key physicochemical property affecting oral absorption and safety.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower molecular weight higher.
payload.falsification_test: If molecular weight does not affect oral bioavailability or safety, the criterion is not useful.

attribute.definition: Topological polar surface area in Å² from RDKit.
attribute.name: Predicted topological polar surface area (TPSA)
attribute.rationale: TPSA is a key determinant of oral absorption and blood-brain barrier penetration.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower TPSA higher.
payload.falsification_test: If TPSA does not affect oral absorption, the criterion is not useful.

attribute.definition: Number of hydrogen bond donors from RDKit.
attribute.name: Predicted hydrogen bond donor count
attribute.rationale: Hydrogen bond donors affect solubility and permeability.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer hydrogen bond donors higher.
payload.falsification_test: If hydrogen bond donor count does not affect oral bioavailability, the criterion is not useful.

attribute.definition: Number of hydrogen bond acceptors from RDKit.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer hydrogen bond acceptors higher.

attribute.definition: Number of rotatable bonds from RDKit.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model. Higher values indicate greater solubility; higher is better.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Aqueous solubility is a key determinant of oral absorption. Claims claim_01M4YWWNDV0J4636YHBMNYEN81 (paclitaxel solubility <0.1 µg/mL restricts oral bioavailability to <10%), claim_01M4YX02VMJ69P0QH60D7MPXQ9 (icariin poor aqueous solubility ~0.02 mg/mL, low oral bioavailability ~12%), and claim_01M4YX7V91K4CFR3TYKM8BRVGV (poor aqueous solubility limits efficacy) establish that low solubility is associated with poor oral bioavailability. The model provides a predicted value for every compound with a structure.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with predicted aqueous solubility >= -4 log(mol/L) above those with lower or unknown values; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with predicted solubility < -4 log(mol/L) is shown to have adequate oral absorption in humans, the cutoff would be falsified.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim reports icariin's aqueous solubility as ~0.02 mg/mL, which is approximately 3.3e-5 mol/L (assuming a molecular weight of ~600 g/mol), i.e., log10(mol/L) ≈ -4.5. This value is associated with low oral bioavailability (~12%). Using -4 log(mol/L) as a preference cutoff ranks candidates with predicted solubility at or above this level above those with lower solubility, without excluding any candidate.

interpretation.measurement: Icariin aqueous solubility is ~0.02 mg/mL, associated with low oral bioavailability.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidate library consists of orally administered kinase inhibitors; a solubility of -4 log(mol/L) is a conservative lower bound for adequate dissolution and absorption, consistent with the reported value for a poorly soluble drug. Candidates at or above this level are preferred.

attribute.definition: Median curated pChEMBL potency (pChEMBL = -log10 molar IC50/Ki/Kd/EC50) for the compound against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844), pooled across ChEMBL and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology curated measurements.
attribute.name: CSF1R curated potency
attribute.rationale: CSF1R is a required target in the objective. Curated potency measurements from ChEMBL and IUPHAR provide the quantitative engagement evidence. Pooling the two independent curations under median aggregation gives the best estimate of central potency.

critic_findings.finding: The cited claims (e.g. claim_01M4X8CBBBZKQQ70JGB7ZYF0ED, claim_01M4X8NA3JZAVD93B23WNZ4EQV) are qualitative target-coverage assertions and do not provide curated pChEMBL potency values for CSF1R, so they do not support the defined quantitative attribute.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by measured CSF1R potency; compounds with higher median pChEMBL rank above those with lower or no measured potency.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with no CSF1R pChEMBL record is later shown to be a potent CSF1R inhibitor, the preference ordering would be misleading; however, the rule does not exclude, so the candidate remains in the pool with unknown status.

attribute.rationale: QED summarizes drug-like properties relevant to safety and developability.

critic_findings.finding: QED drug-likeness is a composite developability score and does not measure engagement of the five targets.
claim_01M4ZH6FH8YH07RTW3YFWVH569 does not support QED or the 0.5 cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher QED higher, favouring agents with more drug-like properties.
payload.falsification_test: If QED does not correlate with developability or safety for kinase inhibitors, the criterion adds no value.

attribute.definition: Number of Lipinski rule of 5 violations computed from the structure, a flag for poor drug-likeness.

claim_01M4ZH6FH8YH07RTW3YFWVH569 does not support Lipinski violations or the <= 1 cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer Lipinski violations higher, favouring agents with better drug-likeness.
payload.falsification_test: If Lipinski violation count does not correlate with developability or safety for kinase inhibitors, the criterion adds no value.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound blocks the hERG potassium channel, a liability for QT prolongation and arrhythmia under chronic oral dosing.
attribute.name: Predicted hERG blocking probability
attribute.rationale: Cardiac safety is a recurring theme in the claims (QT prolongation, arrhythmias, HF). The hERG model is the only computable cardiac liability endpoint available and covers every compound with a structure.

critic_findings.finding: Cited claims describe QT prolongation via PI3K inhibition by osimertinib and general cardiac ion-channel effects; none establish that hERG channel blocking probability is the operative liability or that a 0.5 model decision boundary is meaningful.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted hERG blockade above those with higher probability, reducing the chance that a QT-prolonging candidate is recommended.
payload.falsification_test: If the top-ranked compound has a predicted hERG probability above 0.5 while a lower-ranked compound has a probability below 0.5, the preference ordering is not being applied.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound causes drug-induced liver injury, a major liability for chronic oral therapy.
attribute.name: Predicted drug-induced liver injury (DILI) probability
attribute.rationale: Hepatotoxicity is a common cause of attrition for chronic oral kinase inhibitors; the DILI model provides a computable surrogate for every compound with a structure.

critic_findings.finding: Cited claims report elevated transaminases and general adverse events but do not establish DILI probability as the operative liability nor support a 0.5 cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted DILI probability above those with higher probability.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with predicted DILI probability above 0.5 outranks one below 0.5, the preference is not being applied.

attribute.definition: Reported absolute or relative oral bioavailability (F%) in humans, as a measured pharmacokinetic parameter. Higher values indicate greater fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation intact.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "oral bioavailability"

attribute.name: Oral bioavailability (human, measured F%)
attribute.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of an oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans. The objective requires oral administration; a measured human F% is the most decision-relevant absorption parameter. Multiple claims report human F% values (e.g., 58%, 38-49%, 85-90%, 21.4%, 4.7%, 69-83%, 25%).

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower values; candidates with F% >= 21.4% receive a preference boost.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with F% < 21.4% is approved and clinically effective as an oral agent for the required targets, the threshold is too stringent.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim reports a measured human oral bioavailability of 21.4% for an orally administered drug. This value is a real-world example of an acceptable human F% for an oral kinase inhibitor, supporting a preference threshold at or above 21.4%.

interpretation.measurement: The passage reports a measured human oral bioavailability of 21.4%.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidate set consists of orally administered kinase inhibitors intended for clinical development. A human F% of at least 21.4% is a reasonable lower bound for adequate systemic exposure, as exemplified by this measured value for an approved oral drug.

attribute.definition: Molecular weight of the compound in Daltons, as computed from structure. Lower values are generally associated with better oral absorption.
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)
attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a key physicochemical determinant of oral absorption. Claims state that most clinically relevant kinase inhibitors fall within 380-500 Da and that drugs with MW < 500 Da have acceptable oral bioavailability. The Lipinski rule of 5 uses MW < 500 Da as a criterion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with MW <= 500 Da above those with higher MW; candidates with MW > 500 Da are penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with MW > 500 Da is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the threshold is too strict.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim explicitly states that drugs with MW < 500 Da have acceptable oral bioavailability, making this a decision threshold for oral absorption.

attribute.definition: Calculated logP (octanol-water partition coefficient). Moderate lipophilicity is optimal for oral absorption.
attribute.name: Lipophilicity (logP)
attribute.rationale: Lipophilicity affects membrane permeability and solubility. Claims state that moderate lipophilicity (logP ~2-4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors and that most FDA-approved smTKIs have logP < 5, with a median of 3.7.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with logP within 2-4 above those outside this range; candidates with logP < 2 or > 4 are penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with logP outside 2-4 is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the range is too narrow.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim states that moderate lipophilicity (logP ~2-4) is considered optimal for kinase inhibitors, providing a heuristic lower bound for oral absorption.

interpretation.measurement: The passage reports a heuristic range of logP 2-4 as optimal for kinase inhibitors.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidate set consists of kinase inhibitors intended for oral administration. The heuristic range is directly applicable to this chemical class.

attribute.definition: Topological polar surface area in Å², computed from structure. Lower TPSA is associated with better oral absorption.
attribute.name: Topological polar surface area (TPSA)
attribute.rationale: TPSA is a key determinant of passive membrane permeability. The claim states that TPSA values below approximately 90 Å² are favorable for oral absorption.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with TPSA <= 90 Å² above those with higher TPSA.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with TPSA > 90 Å² is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the threshold is too strict.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim states that TPSA values below approximately 90 Å² are favorable for oral absorption, providing a heuristic upper bound.

interpretation.measurement: The passage reports a heuristic threshold of TPSA < 90 Å² for oral absorption.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidate set consists of orally administered kinase inhibitors. The heuristic is directly applicable to this chemical class.

attribute.definition: Number of Lipinski rule of 5 violations (MW > 500, logP > 5, HBD > 5, HBA > 10). Lower counts indicate better drug-likeness and oral absorption potential.
attribute.name: Lipinski rule of 5 compliance (count of violations)
attribute.rationale: The Lipinski rule of 5 is a widely used heuristic for oral bioavailability. The claim states that drugs with MW < 500, logP < 5, HBA <= 10, and HBD <= 5 have acceptable oral bioavailability. The endpoint returns the count of violations.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with fewer Lipinski violations above those with more, without a numeric cutoff.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with more Lipinski violations is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the ordering is not informative.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of P-glycoprotein inhibition. Lower probability is preferred to avoid efflux-mediated reduction in oral absorption.
attribute.name: P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-glycoprotein efflux limits oral absorption. The claim states that overexpression of efflux transporters such as P-gp limits intracellular drug accumulation. The model has high held-out AUPRC (0.9581) and AUROC (0.9475).

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower P-gp inhibition probability above those with higher probability, without a numeric cutoff.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with high P-gp inhibition probability is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the ordering is not informative.

attribute.definition: Time to reach maximum plasma concentration after oral administration, in hours. Shorter times indicate faster absorption.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "Tmax"

attribute.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax)
attribute.rationale: Tmax is a measure of the rate of oral absorption. Claims report Tmax values ranging from 1 to 12 hours for various oral drugs. Faster absorption (lower Tmax) is generally preferred for oral drugs.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with shorter Tmax above those with longer Tmax, without a numeric cutoff.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with longer Tmax is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the ordering is not informative.

attribute.definition: Whether the compound is documented as orally administered in humans (e.g., approved oral drug, clinical trial oral dosing).
attribute.name: Oral administration route (recorded)
attribute.rationale: The task requires oral administration. This attribute records whether the compound has a documented oral route in humans, which is a prerequisite for the objective. The route flag is a boolean; absence before approval gives unknown, never fail.

payload.expected_change: Excludes candidates without documented oral administration; only candidates with oral=true proceed.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate without a documented oral route is later found to be orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the exclusion is too strict.

attribute.definition: Absolute oral bioavailability (F%) measured in humans, as reported in peer-reviewed literature or regulatory reviews. Higher values indicate a larger fraction of the oral dose reaching systemic circulation.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("oral bioavailability" OR "absolute bioavailability" OR "F%") AND (human OR clinical)

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
attribute.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of an oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans, the most clinically relevant absorption parameter. The cited claims report human F% values (4.7% and 98%) that illustrate the wide range of reported values but do not themselves establish a minimum acceptable F% or a ranking basis; no source-stated cutoff is present, so the rule ranks by value as a preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower values, favouring compounds with better absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with low measured human F% (e.g., <10%) is clinically effective orally at tolerated doses, the preference for high F% would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility from the ADMET-AI model (Solubility_AqSolDB endpoint) in log(mol/L). Higher values indicate greater solubility.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Aqueous solubility is required for dissolution in gastrointestinal fluid, a prerequisite for oral absorption. The ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model has held-out R2 0.8166, a good regression predictor, and is computable for every compound with a structure. Used as a preference to rank candidates by predicted solubility. No source-stated cutoff exists for this model output, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted aqueous solubility above those with lower values, favouring compounds that can dissolve for absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted solubility (< -6 log mol/L) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the model's utility as a preference would be questioned.

attribute.definition: Predicted cell effective permeability from the ADMET-AI model (Caco2_Wang endpoint) in log(10^-6 cm/s). Higher values indicate greater permeability.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)
attribute.rationale: Intestinal permeability is a key determinant of oral absorption. The ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang model has held-out R2 0.7065, a moderate regression predictor, and is computable for every compound with a structure. Used as a preference to rank candidates by predicted permeability. No source-stated cutoff exists for this model output, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted Caco-2 permeability above those with lower values, favouring compounds likely to cross the intestinal epithelium.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted Caco-2 permeability (< -6 log 10^-6 cm/s) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the model's utility as a preference would be questioned.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of P-glycoprotein inhibition from the ADMET-AI model (Pgp_Broccatelli endpoint) in [0,1]. Higher values indicate a higher likelihood of P-gp inhibition, which may reduce oral absorption of co-administered drugs but is not directly a property of the candidate's own absorption.
attribute.name: P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-glycoprotein efflux can limit oral absorption. The ADMET-AI Pgp_Broccatelli model has held-out AUROC 0.9475, a strong classifier, and is computable for every compound with a structure. Used as a preference to rank candidates with lower predicted P-gp inhibition higher, as this may correlate with better absorption. No source-stated cutoff exists for this model output, so the rule ranks by value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower predicted P-gp inhibition probability above those with higher values, favouring compounds less likely to be effluxed.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high predicted P-gp inhibition probability (>0.8) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the model's utility as a preference would be questioned.

attribute.definition: Molecular weight in Daltons, computed from the structure. Lower values are generally associated with better passive diffusion and oral absorption.
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)
attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a critical determinant of passive diffusion and oral bioavailability. The cited claims state that most clinically relevant kinase inhibitors fall within approximately 380-500 Da, a descriptive range rather than a required cutoff, and that excessive MW reduces intestinal absorption. No source-stated maximum acceptable MW is present, so the rule ranks by value as a preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower molecular weight above those with higher values, favouring compounds with better passive diffusion.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high molecular weight (>500 Da) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for lower MW would be weakened.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The source offers logP ≈ 2–4 as the optimal range for kinase inhibitors; the lower edge is the heuristic line below which lipophilicity is suboptimal for passive diffusion.

interpretation.measurement: logP ≈ 2–4 is considered optimal for kinase inhibitors
