interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are kinase inhibitors being screened for oral developability, the same class the heuristic addresses.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The source offers logP ≈ 2–4 as the optimal range for kinase inhibitors; the upper edge is the heuristic line above which lipophilicity compromises solubility and increases clearance.

interpretation.measurement: logP ≈ 2–4 is considered optimal for kinase inhibitors
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are kinase inhibitors being screened for oral developability, the same class the heuristic addresses.

attribute.definition: Computed XLogP (log units) from PubChem. The source states moderate lipophilicity (logP ≈ 2–4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors; candidates are ranked by distance outside this band, with values inside the band scoring best.
attribute.name: Lipophilicity (logP) within optimal kinase-inhibitor range
attribute.rationale: Moderate lipophilicity (logP ≈ 2–4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors (claim_01M4YGKFT8T97H08A3RS5A2H24); excessive lipophilicity causes poor solubility and increased metabolic clearance (claim_01M4YGKFTX7A37M77HHQX99A1P). The range is a heuristic, so this is a preference ranking by distance outside the band, not a hard exclusion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with logP closer to the 2–4 range above those outside it, favouring compounds with optimal lipophilicity for oral absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with logP outside 2–4 are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for the 2–4 range would be weakened.

attribute.definition: Absolute or relative oral bioavailability measured in humans, expressed as percent of administered dose reaching systemic circulation. Values are pooled across sources reporting a human F% for the compound.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "oral bioavailability"

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
attribute.rationale: The task requires oral administration; measured human F% is the most direct evidence of adequate oral absorption. Claim_01M4YGXW3G7712TV7ZPB5Y5F9A reports 4.7% absolute bioavailability for a compound, demonstrating that human F% is measurable and decision-relevant, but it does not establish a threshold. Used as a preference ordering: higher measured F% ranks above lower or unknown values.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower or unknown values, favouring compounds with demonstrated clinical absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with low or unknown human F% achieves comparable target engagement and clinical efficacy to one with high F%, the preference is not decision-relevant.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the TDC Bioavailability_Ma classifier (AUROC 0.7164). A model prediction, not a measurement.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al. model)
attribute.rationale: Provides a computed oral bioavailability probability for every compound with a structure, covering candidates lacking measured human F%. The model's AUROC of 0.7164 is modest but sufficient for a preference ranking, not a hard exclusion. This replaces the previous literature-bound attribute that lacked supporting measured values.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted oral bioavailability probability above those with lower values, extending absorption assessment to compounds without measured human data.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted probabilities do not correlate with measured human F% in this compound set, the preference adds noise rather than signal.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the TDC Bioavailability_Ma classifier (AUROC 0.7164). A model prediction, not a measurement.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al. model)
attribute.rationale: Provides a computed oral bioavailability probability for every compound with a structure, covering candidates lacking measured human F%. The model's AUROC of 0.7164 is modest but sufficient for a preference ranking, not a hard exclusion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted oral bioavailability probability above those with lower values, extending absorption assessment to compounds without measured human data.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted probabilities do not correlate with measured human F% in this compound set, the preference adds noise rather than signal.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability of human intestinal absorption from the TDC HIA_Hou classifier (AUROC 0.994). A model prediction of the absorption step, not systemic bioavailability.
attribute.name: Human intestinal absorption (HIA) probability
attribute.rationale: High-accuracy model (AUROC 0.994) for the intestinal absorption step. A compound with low HIA probability is unlikely to be orally absorbed, though it may still have high F% if first-pass metabolism is minimal. Useful as a preference to flag absorption-limited candidates.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted HIA probability above those with lower values, favouring compounds likely to cross the intestinal epithelium.
payload.falsification_test: If candidates with low HIA probability still achieve adequate systemic exposure via oral dosing, the preference is not decision-relevant.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility from the TDC Solubility_AqSolDB regression model (R² 0.8166). Higher values indicate greater solubility, which supports dissolution and absorption after oral dosing.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Solubility is a prerequisite for oral absorption. The model has good regression performance (R² 0.8166). Low solubility can limit absorption even for permeable compounds. A preference, not a hard exclusion, because formulation can mitigate poor solubility.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted aqueous solubility above those with lower values, favouring compounds that can dissolve in the gastrointestinal tract.
payload.falsification_test: If poorly soluble candidates achieve adequate oral absorption through formulation or high permeability, the preference is not decision-relevant.

attribute.definition: Predicted effective permeability across Caco-2 cell monolayers from the TDC Caco2_Wang regression model (R² 0.7065). Higher values indicate greater intestinal permeability.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)
attribute.rationale: Caco-2 permeability is a standard in vitro surrogate for intestinal absorption. The model's R² of 0.7065 is moderate. Useful as a preference to rank candidates by likely absorption efficiency.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted Caco-2 permeability above those with lower values, favouring compounds likely to cross the intestinal barrier.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted Caco-2 permeability does not correlate with measured human absorption for this compound set, the preference adds noise.

attribute.definition: ChEMBL molecule record flag indicating whether the compound is documented as orally administered. Categorical boolean: true if oral route is recorded, false if not, unknown if the field is empty. A true value ranks the candidate above one with no recorded oral flag; a false value ranks below.
attribute.name: Oral administration route (recorded) preference
attribute.rationale: The task constraint requires oral administration, and the cited claims show oral agents exist in the library (ivosidenib is oral; sorafenib is an oral antiangiogenic). A recorded oral flag is direct evidence of the required route, so it should rank candidates, but absence of a flag is unknown rather than a failure, so this is a preference, not a hard exclusion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with a recorded oral flag of true above those with unknown or false flags; no candidate is excluded.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with a recorded oral flag of false is later shown to be orally administered and clinically effective, the preference would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Measured human oral bioavailability (F%) compared against a threshold of 10%, below which oral administration is unlikely to achieve therapeutic systemic exposure. Values are measured in clinical or human PK studies. Higher values rank above lower values.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("oral bioavailability" OR "absolute bioavailability" OR "F%") AND (human OR clinical OR patient)

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%) preference
attribute.rationale: A threshold at 10% is a conservative minimum below which oral administration is unlikely to be viable. The cited claims report human F% values of 57%, 39% and 3.5%, with the low values described as poor or inadequate, supporting 10% as a heuristic line rather than a stated requirement. The registry already contains 'Human oral bioavailability (measured F%) threshold'; this proposal is distinct in using a preference rule with a 10% cutoff and a bound_support record declaring the heuristic interpretation.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with measured human F% >= 10% above those with lower values; candidates with unknown F% are not excluded but rank lower.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with measured human F% < 10% achieves clinical efficacy at an oral dose, the 10% preference would be falsified as a decision-relevant cutoff.

attribute.definition: Fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation unchanged, measured in humans and reported as a percentage. Values are pooled across independent human studies; the median is taken when several measurements exist.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("oral bioavailability" OR "absolute bioavailability" OR "fraction absorbed") AND (human OR patient OR volunteer)

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
attribute.rationale: The task requires oral administration; measured human F% is the most direct evidence that a candidate achieves systemic exposure after oral dosing. The literature route is the only catalog entry that can return measured human F% values. No cited claim states a general numeric threshold for adequate oral exposure, so the rule ranks candidates by F% rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Candidates with higher measured human F% rank above those with lower or unknown F%; candidates with no human F% data are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If measured human F% does not correlate with clinical oral efficacy across the library, the ordering is falsified as a useful preference.

attribute.definition: ChEMBL molecule record flag indicating that the compound is administered orally. A boolean; true means oral administration is recorded.
attribute.name: Oral administration route (recorded)
attribute.rationale: The task constraint states oral administration is required. A recorded oral route flag is direct evidence that the compound has been developed for oral dosing. The flag is often empty before approval, which gives unknown, never fail. No numeric cutoff is applicable; the rule is a categorical preference for a true flag.

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a recorded oral route flag rank above those without; missing flags are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate without a recorded oral flag is later approved for oral use, the preference for the flag is falsified as a useful discriminator.

attribute.definition: Computed molecular weight from PubChem (property_estimate).
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)
attribute.rationale: Lipinski's rule of 5 suggests MW < 500 Da for acceptable oral bioavailability (claim_01M4YV82RH8W5DSY15E37TJQC3). The claim states this as a guideline for acceptable oral bioavailability, so it is used as a preference cutoff rather than a hard exclusion, because many approved kinase inhibitors exceed this value.

payload.expected_change: Candidates with MW <= 500 g/mol rank above those with higher values; missing values are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with MW > 500 Da is orally bioavailable, the preference may be misleading.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim states that drugs with MW < 500 Da have acceptable oral bioavailability as per Lipinski's Rule, a widely accepted guideline for predicting oral bioavailability. The candidate library consists of orally intended small-molecule kinase inhibitors, so the guideline applies as a preference for lower molecular weight.

attribute.definition: ChEMBL molecule record flag indicating whether the drug is administered orally (boolean).
attribute.name: Oral administration route (recorded)
attribute.rationale: The task constraint explicitly requires oral administration. A recorded oral flag is direct evidence of oral dosing feasibility. Absence of a record gives unknown, which blocks recommendation because the hard requirement cannot be confirmed.

payload.expected_change: Candidates without a recorded oral flag are excluded from recommendation.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate without a recorded oral flag is known to be orally administered, the hard exclusion would be invalid.

attribute.definition: Fold-change in AUC due to food effect on oral absorption, as reported in clinical pharmacology studies or labels. A value of 1 indicates no food effect; values greater than 1 indicate increased exposure with food.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("food effect" OR "fasted" OR "fed") AND (pharmacokinetics OR absorption)

attribute.name: Food effect on AUC (fold-change)
attribute.rationale: Food effects can significantly alter oral exposure and complicate dosing. A smaller fold-change (closer to 1) is preferred for clinical development. The cited claims report food effects for specific agents, but no universal cutoff is stated, so this remains an exploratory consideration.

payload.expected_change: Candidates with smaller food-effect fold-changes are noted as more favorable.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with a significant food effect can be managed with dietary instructions without compromising efficacy, the consideration would be less important.

attribute.definition: Fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation unchanged in humans, as reported in peer-reviewed clinical pharmacokinetic studies. Values are percentages; higher is better.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("oral bioavailability" OR "absolute bioavailability") AND (human OR clinical)

attribute.name: Human oral bioavailability (measured F%)
attribute.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans, the most decision-relevant absorption property for an orally administered agent. Claims claim_01M4YWSBEFTHXZ1719VA2XSKBQ (3-4%), claim_01M4YWWNDV0J4636YHBMNYEN81 (<10%), claim_01M4YX02TZ6J8HRH8GP1CH611E (~12%) and claim_01M4YX02VMJ69P0QH60D7MPXQ9 (~12%) report measured human oral bioavailability values, establishing that this quantity is reported and can be thresholded.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with measured human oral bioavailability >=10% above those with lower or unknown values; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with measured oral bioavailability <10% is later shown to achieve adequate systemic exposure and clinical efficacy, the cutoff would be falsified.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim reports that paclitaxel's oral bioavailability is restricted to below 10% due to poor water solubility. The passage reports an observed value, not a stated requirement; the step from that observation to a screening line is an interpretation. Applying >=10% as a preference cutoff ranks candidates with adequate oral exposure above those with negligible absorption, without excluding any candidate outright.

interpretation.measurement: Paclitaxel oral bioavailability is below 10%.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidate library consists of orally administered kinase inhibitors; a 10% oral bioavailability threshold is a conservative lower bound for adequate systemic exposure, consistent with the reported value for a poorly absorbed drug. Candidates at or above this level are preferred.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound is absorbed from the human gastrointestinal tract, from the ADMET-AI HIA_Hou classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher is better.
attribute.name: Human intestinal absorption (HIA) probability
attribute.rationale: Intestinal absorption is a prerequisite for oral bioavailability. The HIA_Hou model provides a probability for every compound with a structure, enabling screening of the full library. Claim claim_01M4YWSBEFTHXZ1719VA2XSKBQ notes that poor absorption contributes to low oral bioavailability, and claim_01M4YWSBFSAB0MBJG2S3KEMC7K states that extremely low oral bioavailability limits clinical application, supporting the relevance of absorption prediction.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted HIA probability above those with lower values; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with predicted HIA probability <0.5 is shown to have adequate oral absorption in humans, the cutoff would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the ADMET-AI Bioavailability_Ma classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher is better.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability probability (Ma et al. model)
attribute.rationale: Directly predicts oral bioavailability, the key absorption property for an orally administered agent. The model covers all compounds with a structure. Claims claim_01M4YWSBEFTHXZ1719VA2XSKBQ and claim_01M4YX02TZ6J8HRH8GP1CH611E report low oral bioavailability as a limiting factor, supporting the need for this prediction.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted oral bioavailability probability above those with lower values; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with predicted oral bioavailability probability <0.5 is shown to have adequate oral bioavailability in humans, the cutoff would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model. Higher values indicate greater solubility; higher is better.
attribute.name: Aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
attribute.rationale: Aqueous solubility is a key determinant of oral absorption. Claims claim_01M4YWWNDV0J4636YHBMNYEN81 (paclitaxel solubility <0.1 µg/mL restricts oral bioavailability to <10%), claim_01M4YX02VMJ69P0QH60D7MPXQ9 (icariin poor aqueous solubility ~0.02 mg/mL, low oral bioavailability ~12%), and claim_01M4YX7V91K4CFR3TYKM8BRVGV (poor aqueous solubility limits efficacy) establish that low solubility is associated with poor oral bioavailability. The model provides a predicted value for every compound with a structure.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted aqueous solubility above those with lower values; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with predicted solubility < -4 log(mol/L) is shown to have adequate oral absorption in humans, the cutoff would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted apparent permeability coefficient across Caco-2 monolayers in log(10^-6 cm/s) from the ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang model. Higher values indicate greater permeability; higher is better.
attribute.name: Caco-2 permeability (log 10^-6 cm/s)
attribute.rationale: Intestinal permeability is a key determinant of oral absorption. Claim claim_01M4YWSBEFTHXZ1719VA2XSKBQ reports that low intestinal permeability (Caco-2 Papp far below high-permeability thresholds) contributes to poor oral bioavailability. The model provides a predicted value for every compound with a structure.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher predicted Caco-2 permeability above those with lower values; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with predicted Caco-2 permeability < -6 log(10^-6 cm/s) is shown to have adequate oral absorption in humans, the cutoff would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound inhibits P-glycoprotein, from the ADMET-AI Pgp_Broccatelli classifier. Values in [0,1]; lower is better (less efflux inhibition).
attribute.name: P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-glycoprotein efflux can limit oral absorption and contribute to drug-drug interactions. Claims claim_01M4YWWNE62Z3334PP3DCXG6PQ (darunavir low oral bioavailability due to P-gp efflux substrate), claim_01M4YWSBFEHJDG6VD869GJA6P4 (efflux transport may contribute to low exposure), and claim_01M4YWP7MVYC2PM11SF24J7BB3 (P-gp inhibition raises toxicity of co-administered drugs) support the relevance of P-gp liability. The model provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower predicted P-gp inhibition probability above those with higher values; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with predicted P-gp inhibition probability >0.5 is shown to have adequate oral absorption and no interaction liability, the cutoff would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Molecular weight in g/mol, computed from the structure. Lower is generally better for oral absorption.
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)
attribute.rationale: Molecular weight is a fundamental physicochemical property influencing oral absorption. Claim claim_01M4YWSBER5SSX5NCN7XJ5Y6B3 notes that quantitative physicochemical descriptors (e.g., logP/logD, polar surface area, hydrogen-bonding capacity) are needed for biopharmaceutic classification, and claim_01M4YXEMHHX0AP060CNRBVTBDQ states that design of inhibitors with appropriate physical properties is critical. The PubChem computed descriptor provides a derived value for every compound with a structure.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower molecular weight above those with higher values; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with molecular weight >500 g/mol is shown to have adequate oral bioavailability, the cutoff would be falsified.

attribute.definition: XLogP, a computed octanol-water partition coefficient, in log units. Higher values indicate greater lipophilicity; lower lipophilicity is generally preferable for oral absorption and for avoiding the poor physical properties noted for this inhibitor class.
attribute.name: Lipophilicity (XLogP)
attribute.rationale: Lipophilicity influences solubility, permeability and metabolic stability. Claim claim_01M4YXEMGPEMDQGGFNCJ2BTR7J notes that KDR inhibitors have typically possessed poor physical properties including low aqueous solubility and high lipophilicity, and claim_01M4YWSBER5SSX5NCN7XJ5Y6B3 lists logP/logD among the physicochemical descriptors needed for biopharmaceutic classification. The PubChem computed descriptor provides a derived value for every compound with a structure. No cited claim states a numeric logP threshold, so the rule ranks by the value rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower XLogP above those with higher XLogP; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with high XLogP is shown to have adequate oral bioavailability and developability, the preference's relevance is weakened.

attribute.definition: Topological polar surface area in Å², computed from the structure. Lower values are generally associated with better oral absorption and permeability.
attribute.name: Topological polar surface area (TPSA)
attribute.rationale: TPSA is a key descriptor for oral absorption and permeability. Claim claim_01M4YWSBER5SSX5NCN7XJ5Y6B3 notes that polar surface area is among the quantitative physicochemical descriptors needed for biopharmaceutic classification. The PubChem computed descriptor provides a derived value for every compound with a structure. No cited claim states a numeric TPSA threshold, so the rule ranks by the value rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower TPSA above those with higher TPSA; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with high TPSA is shown to have adequate oral bioavailability, the preference's relevance is weakened.

attribute.definition: Number of Lipinski rule-of-five violations (molecular weight >500, logP >5, hydrogen bond donors >5, hydrogen bond acceptors >10), computed from the structure. Lower is better.
attribute.name: Lipinski rule of 5 compliance (count of violations)
attribute.rationale: Lipinski rule-of-five compliance is a standard heuristic for oral bioavailability. Claim claim_01M4YXEMHHX0AP060CNRBVTBDQ states that design of inhibitors with appropriate physical properties is critical, and claim_01M4YWSBER5SSX5NCN7XJ5Y6B3 notes the need for physicochemical descriptors. The ADMET-AI Lipinski endpoint provides a count of violations for every compound with a structure. No cited claim states a numeric violation threshold, so the rule ranks by the value rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with fewer Lipinski violations above those with more; unknown values receive no penalty.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with more Lipinski violations is shown to have adequate oral bioavailability, the preference's relevance is weakened.

attribute.definition: Number of rotatable bonds computed from the structure. Lower counts indicate reduced conformational flexibility, which is associated with improved passive diffusion across biological membranes and more favorable pharmacokinetic profiles.
attribute.name: Rotatable bond count
attribute.rationale: Reduced conformational flexibility is associated with improved passive diffusion and favorable pharmacokinetics (claim_01M4XPWAK6CGBR7K32B1PDYDTA). The descriptor is computed for every compound with a structure. This is a useful preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by rotatable bond count; lower counts are preferred.
payload.falsification_test: If rotatable bond count does not correlate with permeability or pharmacokinetics, the preference should be discarded.

attribute.definition: Number of heavy atoms computed from the structure. Lower counts are generally preferred for drug-likeness.
attribute.name: Heavy atom count
attribute.rationale: Heavy atom count is a measure of molecular size. The descriptor is computed for every compound with a structure. This is a useful preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by heavy atom count; lower counts are preferred.
payload.falsification_test: If heavy atom count does not correlate with drug-likeness, the preference should be discarded.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted topological polar surface area (TPSA), a descriptor of molecular polarity that the cited source associates with passive diffusion and CNS penetration.
attribute.name: Predicted topological polar surface area (TPSA)
attribute.rationale: The cited claim states that TPSA values below approximately 90 Å² correlate with improved CNS penetration. This is a heuristic about CNS penetration, not a stated requirement for oral absorption. It is retained as a preference because lower polarity is generally favorable for passive diffusion, and the applicability to this candidate population is declared as an inference rather than a claim the source makes about oral absorption.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted TPSA higher, favoring better passive diffusion, with the CNS-penetration context of the cited heuristic stated explicitly.
payload.falsification_test: If TPSA does not correlate with passive diffusion or oral absorption for kinase inhibitors, the criterion's utility is falsified.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim states that TPSA values below approximately 90 Å² correlate with improved CNS penetration. The task screens orally administered kinase inhibitors for tumour-microenvironment targets, not CNS targets, so the source's stated context is CNS penetration. The step from that context to this candidate population is an inference: lower TPSA supports passive diffusion, which is relevant to oral absorption, but the source does not state the 90 Å² line as an oral-absorption requirement. The bound is therefore declared as a heuristic line applied by inference, not as a threshold the source states for this population.

interpretation.measurement: The passage reports that TPSA values below approximately 90 Å² correlate with improved CNS penetration.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are orally administered kinase inhibitors; lower TPSA supports passive diffusion, which is relevant to oral absorption, but the source's stated context is CNS penetration, so the step to this population is an inference and the rule is a preference, not a hard exclusion.

validator_problems: units: units: quantitative attribute 'Predicted topological polar surface area (TPSA)' has no unit
units: route predicted_property_lookup/admet_prediction returns 'Å²', but the attribute declares None; the assessor has no registered conversion in that direction

attribute.definition: Model-predicted number of hydrogen bond donors, influencing membrane permeability and solubility.
attribute.name: Predicted hydrogen bond donor count
attribute.rationale: A limited number of hydrogen bonding interactions correlates with improved passive diffusion. Lower donor count is preferred. No numeric cutoff is asserted because the cited claim states no donor-count threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer hydrogen bond donors higher, favoring better passive diffusion.
payload.falsification_test: If hydrogen bond donor count does not correlate with permeability for kinase inhibitors, the criterion's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted number of hydrogen bond acceptors, influencing membrane permeability and solubility.
attribute.name: Predicted hydrogen bond acceptor count
attribute.rationale: A limited number of hydrogen bonding interactions correlates with improved passive diffusion. Lower acceptor count is preferred. No numeric cutoff is asserted because the cited claim states no acceptor-count threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer hydrogen bond acceptors higher, favoring better passive diffusion.
payload.falsification_test: If hydrogen bond acceptor count does not correlate with permeability for kinase inhibitors, the criterion's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Computed number of rotatable bonds, a measure of molecular flexibility influencing oral bioavailability.
attribute.name: Rotatable bond count
attribute.rationale: Molecular flexibility, estimated by rotatable bonds, is a determinant of oral bioavailability. Lower counts are generally preferred. No numeric cutoff is asserted because the cited claim states no threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer rotatable bonds higher, favoring better oral bioavailability.
payload.falsification_test: If rotatable bond count does not correlate with oral bioavailability for kinase inhibitors, the criterion's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Computed number of heavy atoms, a measure of molecular size.
attribute.name: Heavy atom count
attribute.rationale: Smaller molecules are generally more likely to have favorable drug-like properties. Lower counts are preferred. No numeric cutoff is asserted because the cited claim states no heavy-atom threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer heavy atoms higher, favoring smaller, more drug-like molecules.
payload.falsification_test: If heavy atom count does not correlate with drug-likeness for kinase inhibitors, the criterion's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound blocks the hERG potassium channel, a liability for QT prolongation and arrhythmia under chronic oral dosing.
attribute.name: Predicted hERG blocking probability
attribute.rationale: hERG blockade is a well-established safety liability for chronic oral kinase inhibitors; the ADMET-AI hERG model (AUROC 0.8388) provides a computable surrogate for every compound with a structure. No numeric cutoff is asserted because the cited claim states no hERG threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted hERG liability higher, reducing the risk of cardiac adverse events during chronic dosing.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted hERG probability still show clinical QT prolongation, the model's utility as a screening preference is falsified.

attribute.definition: Computed molecular weight in g/mol, a physicochemical determinant of oral absorption and drug-likeness for small-molecule kinase inhibitors.
attribute.name: Computed molecular weight
attribute.rationale: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors are usually smaller than 500 Da, allowing efficient membrane penetration and oral administration (claim_01M4YJEH73WNH562K7XZR6TAMA). This is a class-level heuristic for the candidate population, used as a preference rather than an exclusion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with molecular weight <=500 Da above those exceeding it.
payload.falsification_test: If the top-ranked compound has molecular weight >500 Da while a lower-ranked compound has <=500 Da, the preference is not discriminating as intended.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim states that small-molecule kinase inhibitors are usually smaller than 500 Da, allowing efficient membrane penetration and oral administration. This is a rule of thumb for the class of orally administered kinase inhibitors, which is the candidate population being screened.

interpretation.measurement: The passage reports that small-molecule kinase inhibitors are usually smaller than 500 Da in molecular weight.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are small-molecule kinase inhibitors intended for oral administration, the same class the heuristic describes, so 500 Da is a defensible preference line for this population.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted intrinsic clearance in human hepatocytes (uL/min/10^6 cells); higher clearance may lead to low exposure and potentially require higher doses, increasing toxicity risk.
attribute.name: Predicted human hepatocyte intrinsic clearance
attribute.rationale: High clearance can necessitate higher doses, potentially increasing toxicity; the model provides a quantitative estimate for all compounds with structures. The cited claim reports a measured hepatocyte clearance value for a compound in this class, which supplies a defensible reference point for a preference cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted hepatocyte clearance above those with higher clearance, favouring candidates with better exposure and potentially lower toxicity.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted hepatocyte clearance does not correlate with observed clearance or toxicity for this class, the preference is not supported.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim reports a measured hepatocyte intrinsic clearance for a compound in the same chemotype/class being screened; using that observed value as an upper preference bound keeps candidates at or below a clearance level already observed in this series.

interpretation.measurement: Mouse hepatocyte intrinsic clearance of 70.6 ± 5.4 uL/min/10^6 cells for a compound in this class, described as high and close to verapamil.
interpretation.population_rationale: Candidates are orally administered kinase inhibitors in the same series; a clearance at or below the reported value is a reasonable preference bound for acceptable exposure, while higher values are disfavoured rather than excluded.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted intrinsic clearance in human liver microsomes (uL/min/mg); higher clearance may lead to low exposure and potentially require higher doses, increasing toxicity risk.
attribute.name: Predicted microsomal intrinsic clearance
attribute.rationale: High microsomal clearance can necessitate higher doses, potentially increasing toxicity; the model provides a quantitative estimate for all compounds with structures. The cited claim supplies a measured clearance value in the same class, used here as a cross-system reference bound for a preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted microsomal clearance above those with higher clearance, favouring candidates with better exposure and potentially lower toxicity.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted microsomal clearance does not correlate with observed clearance or toxicity for this class, the preference is not supported.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The claim reports a measured hepatocyte intrinsic clearance for a compound in this class; the same numeric value is used as a preference bound on the microsomal clearance scale because both express intrinsic clearance in the same class and the bound is a ranking preference, not an exclusion.

interpretation.measurement: Mouse hepatocyte intrinsic clearance of 70.6 ± 5.4 uL/min/10^6 cells for a compound in this class, described as high.
interpretation.population_rationale: Candidates are orally administered kinase inhibitors in the same series; a microsomal clearance at or below the reported hepatocyte value is a reasonable preference bound for acceptable exposure, while higher values are disfavoured rather than excluded.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted aqueous solubility (log mol/L); higher values indicate better solubility, which favours oral absorption and may reduce dose requirements.
attribute.name: Predicted aqueous solubility
attribute.rationale: Adequate solubility is important for oral absorption and to avoid high doses; the model provides a quantitative estimate for all compounds with structures. The cited claim reports a measured solubility range for a specific compound, not a universal threshold, so the attribute ranks rather than excludes.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted solubility above those with lower solubility, favouring better absorption and potentially lower doses.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted solubility does not correlate with observed solubility or oral absorption for this class, the preference is not supported.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted lipophilicity (log units); lower values are preferred because high lipophilicity is associated with increased metabolism, off-target binding, and toxicity.
attribute.name: Predicted lipophilicity (Lipophilicity_AstraZeneca)
attribute.rationale: High lipophilicity is associated with promiscuity and toxicity; the model provides a quantitative estimate for all compounds with structures. The cited claim reports a measured clogP for a specific compound, not a universal threshold, so the attribute ranks rather than excludes.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted lipophilicity above those with higher lipophilicity, reducing off-target toxicity risk.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted lipophilicity does not correlate with observed lipophilicity or toxicity for this class, the preference is not supported.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted Caco-2 cell permeability (log(10^-6 cm/s)); higher values indicate better permeability, which favours oral absorption and may reduce dose requirements.
attribute.name: Predicted Caco-2 permeability
attribute.rationale: Adequate permeability is important for oral absorption; the model provides a quantitative estimate for all compounds with structures. The cited claim reports a measured permeability for a specific compound, not a universal threshold, so the attribute ranks rather than excludes.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted Caco-2 permeability above those with lower permeability, favouring better absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted Caco-2 permeability does not correlate with observed permeability or oral absorption for this class, the preference is not supported.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of human intestinal absorption; higher values indicate better absorption, which favours oral bioavailability and may reduce dose requirements.
attribute.name: Predicted human intestinal absorption probability
attribute.rationale: Adequate intestinal absorption is essential for oral dosing; the model provides a probability for all compounds with structures. The cited claim reports a measured permeability for a specific compound, not a universal threshold, so the attribute ranks rather than excludes.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted intestinal absorption above those with lower probability, favouring better oral absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted intestinal absorption does not correlate with observed absorption for this class, the preference is not supported.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of oral bioavailability; higher values indicate better oral exposure, which favours clinical development.
attribute.name: Predicted oral bioavailability probability (Bioavailability_Ma)
attribute.rationale: Adequate oral bioavailability is essential for oral dosing; the model provides a probability for all compounds with structures. The cited claim reports a measured permeability for a specific compound, not a universal threshold, so the attribute ranks rather than excludes.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted oral bioavailability above those with lower probability, favouring better oral exposure.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted oral bioavailability does not correlate with observed bioavailability for this class, the preference is not supported.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that a compound has high passive permeability in the PAMPA assay; higher values indicate better passive permeability, which favours oral absorption.
attribute.name: Predicted PAMPA passive permeability probability
attribute.rationale: Adequate passive permeability is important for oral absorption; the model provides a probability for all compounds with structures. The cited claim reports a measured permeability for a specific compound, not a universal threshold, so the attribute ranks rather than excludes.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted PAMPA permeability probability above those with lower probability, favouring better passive absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted PAMPA permeability does not correlate with observed permeability for this class, the preference is not supported.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted hydration free energy (kcal/mol); more negative values indicate better solubility, which is favourable for oral absorption and reducing dose requirements.
attribute.name: Predicted hydration free energy
attribute.rationale: Hydration free energy is related to solubility; more negative values are favourable for oral absorption. The cited claim reports a measured solubility range for a specific compound, not a universal threshold, so the attribute ranks rather than excludes.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with more negative predicted hydration free energy above those with less negative values, favouring better solubility.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted hydration free energy does not correlate with observed solubility for this class, the preference is not supported.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits P-glycoprotein, an efflux transporter; higher probability indicates greater transporter-mediated drug-drug interaction liability.
attribute.name: Predicted P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-glycoprotein inhibition is a documented DDI liability for kinase inhibitors (claim_01M4YVW3GE6XJKPZJ0KW8NG6AD). The cited claim reports that several agents are P-gp inhibitors but states no numeric threshold, so the criterion ranks candidates by predicted probability rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted P-gp inhibition higher, reducing transporter-mediated DDI risk.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted P-gp inhibition still cause clinically significant transporter DDIs, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted aqueous solubility; higher values indicate better solubility and lower risk of absorption-limited exposure.
attribute.name: Predicted aqueous solubility
attribute.rationale: Low aqueous solubility is a documented absorption-limiting liability for kinase inhibitors and related agents (claim_01M4YW08WB13P88KFBYE6GZ2ST, claim_01M4YW4WY5JY8NHSDF23WT3KC5). The cited claims report low solubility for specific compounds but state no numeric threshold, so the criterion ranks candidates by predicted solubility rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted solubility higher, favoring better absorption and exposure.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high predicted solubility still show poor absorption, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted lipophilicity; higher values indicate greater lipophilicity and associated risks of poor solubility and metabolic liability.
attribute.name: Predicted lipophilicity (Lipophilicity_AstraZeneca)
attribute.rationale: High lipophilicity is associated with poor solubility and food-dependent absorption for this drug class (claim_01M4YVW3GTENG97ZF5TZC6PGH6). The cited claim states no numeric threshold, so the criterion ranks candidates by predicted lipophilicity rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted lipophilicity higher, reducing metabolic and toxicity liabilities.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted lipophilicity still show metabolic or toxicity issues, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted Caco-2 cell permeability; higher values indicate greater permeability and lower risk of absorption-limited exposure.
attribute.name: Predicted Caco-2 permeability
attribute.rationale: Permeability is a key determinant of oral absorption and exposure (claim_01M4YW6M2CRXRXJKW7WGYND5XX). The cited claim states no numeric threshold, so the criterion ranks candidates by predicted permeability rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted permeability higher, favoring better absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high predicted permeability still show poor absorption, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of human intestinal absorption; higher probability indicates greater absorption and lower risk of poor oral exposure.
attribute.name: Predicted human intestinal absorption probability
attribute.rationale: Intestinal absorption is a key determinant of oral bioavailability and exposure (claim_01M4YW6M2CRXRXJKW7WGYND5XX). The cited claim states no numeric threshold, so the criterion ranks candidates by predicted absorption probability rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted intestinal absorption higher, favoring better oral exposure.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high predicted absorption still show poor oral exposure, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of oral bioavailability; higher probability indicates better oral exposure.
attribute.name: Predicted oral bioavailability probability (Bioavailability_Ma)
attribute.rationale: Oral bioavailability is essential for an orally administered agent; low bioavailability can lead to variable exposure and toxicity (claim_01M4YW4WY5JY8NHSDF23WT3KC5). The cited claim reports low bioavailability for a specific compound but states no numeric threshold applicable to the model, so the criterion ranks candidates by predicted bioavailability rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted oral bioavailability higher, favoring better oral exposure.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high predicted bioavailability still show poor oral exposure, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of passive permeability in the PAMPA assay; higher probability indicates greater passive permeability and lower risk of absorption-limited exposure.
attribute.name: Predicted PAMPA permeability
attribute.rationale: Passive permeability is a determinant of oral absorption (claim_01M4YW6M2CRXRXJKW7WGYND5XX). The cited claim states no numeric threshold, so the criterion ranks candidates by predicted passive permeability rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted passive permeability higher, favoring better absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high predicted PAMPA permeability still show poor absorption, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted hydration free energy; more negative values indicate better solubility, while very positive values indicate poor solubility.
attribute.name: Predicted hydration free energy
attribute.rationale: Hydration free energy relates to solubility and absorption; poor solubility is a documented issue for this drug class (claim_01M4YW08WB13P88KFBYE6GZ2ST). The cited claim states no numeric threshold, so the criterion ranks candidates by predicted hydration free energy rather than applying a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with more negative hydration free energy higher, favoring better solubility.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with favorable hydration free energy still show poor solubility, the model's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted molecular weight (RDKit); lower values are preferred because high molecular weight is associated with impaired passive intestinal permeation.
attribute.name: Predicted molecular weight
attribute.rationale: The cited claim reports that a compound with molecular weight 610.5 Da cannot permeate the intestinal epithelium via passive diffusion, supporting lower molecular weight as a preference for oral absorption. No cutoff is asserted because the claim does not propose 610.5 Da as a general threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted molecular weight higher, favoring better passive absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted molecular weight still show poor oral absorption, the rule's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted logP (RDKit); lower values are preferred because lipophilic, poorly soluble agents show food-dependent and variable oral absorption.
attribute.name: Predicted logP (RDKit)
attribute.rationale: The cited claim reports that lipophilic, poorly soluble agents have food-dependent absorption, supporting lower lipophilicity as a preference for consistent oral exposure. No cutoff is asserted because the claim states no logP number.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted logP higher, favoring more consistent oral absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted logP still show food-dependent or variable absorption, the rule's utility is falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound blocks the hERG potassium channel; lower values are preferred because hERG blockade is a liability for QT prolongation on chronic oral dosing.
attribute.name: Predicted hERG blocking probability
attribute.rationale: The cited claim reports that a pooled analysis at doses of 0.5-60 mg showed no significant increase in QTc intervals, supporting lower QT-prolongation liability as a preference. No cutoff is asserted because the claim states no hERG probability number.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted hERG blockade higher, reducing the chance of selecting a QT-prolonging agent.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted hERG probability show no difference in QT prolongation in vivo, the criterion is not useful.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of drug-induced liver injury; lower values are preferred because hepatotoxicity is a major safety concern for chronic oral therapy.
attribute.name: Predicted drug-induced liver injury (DILI) probability
attribute.rationale: The cited claims report elevated aminotransferase incidence in treated patients, supporting lower hepatotoxicity liability as a preference. No cutoff is asserted because the claims state no DILI probability number.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted DILI probability higher, reducing hepatotoxicity risk.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted DILI probability does not correlate with clinical hepatotoxicity for kinase inhibitors, the criterion is not useful.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of P-glycoprotein inhibition (Pgp_Broccatelli endpoint); higher values indicate greater likelihood of P-gp inhibition, a drug-drug interaction liability.
attribute.name: Predicted P-glycoprotein inhibition probability
attribute.rationale: P-gp inhibition can cause drug-drug interactions and alter exposure of co-administered oral agents; the model (AUROC 0.9475) is computable for every compound with a structure. Retained as a preference, not an exclusion, because it is a predicted value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted P-gp inhibition higher.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted P-gp inhibition does not correlate with clinical DDIs, the criterion is not useful.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound blocks the hERG potassium channel (hERG endpoint); higher values indicate greater QT-prolongation liability under chronic oral dosing.
attribute.name: Predicted hERG blocking probability
attribute.rationale: Cardiac safety is a chronic-dosing liability for kinase inhibitors; the hERG model (AUROC 0.8388) gives a computable surrogate for QT risk across the whole library. Retained as a preference, not an exclusion, because it is a predicted value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted hERG blockade higher, reducing the chance that a QT-prolonging agent is recommended for chronic oral use.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted hERG probability show no better cardiac safety in the evidence, the criterion adds no discrimination.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of drug-induced liver injury (DILI endpoint); higher values indicate greater hepatotoxicity liability, a class-wide concern for kinase inhibitors.
attribute.name: Predicted drug-induced liver injury (DILI) probability
attribute.rationale: Hepatotoxicity is described as a class-wide liability of protein kinase inhibitors; the DILI model (AUROC 0.8815) provides a computable surrogate. Retained as a preference, not an exclusion, because it is a predicted value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted DILI probability higher, reducing the chance of recommending a hepatotoxic agent for chronic oral dosing.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted DILI probability does not correlate with observed hepatotoxicity for kinase inhibitors, the criterion is uninformative.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of clinical toxicity (ClinTox endpoint: trial failure due to toxicity or FDA boxed warning); higher values indicate greater clinical toxicity liability.
attribute.name: Predicted clinical toxicity probability (ClinTox)
attribute.rationale: Clinical toxicity is a broad safety endpoint relevant to chronic dosing; the ClinTox model (AUROC 0.9275) provides a computable surrogate. Retained as a preference, not an exclusion, because it is a predicted value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted clinical toxicity higher, favouring agents more likely to be tolerable in chronic oral use.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted ClinTox probability does not distinguish clinically tolerated from toxic kinase inhibitors, the criterion adds no value.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of mutagenicity in the Ames test (AMES endpoint); higher values indicate greater genotoxicity liability relevant to chronic dosing.
attribute.name: Predicted mutagenicity probability (AMES)
attribute.rationale: Genotoxicity is a chronic-dosing concern; the AMES model (AUROC 0.8816) provides a computable surrogate. Retained as a preference, not an exclusion, because it is a predicted value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted mutagenicity higher, reducing the chance of recommending a genotoxic agent for chronic oral use.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted AMES probability does not correlate with observed mutagenicity for kinase inhibitors, the criterion is uninformative.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of carcinogenicity (Carcinogens_Lagunin endpoint); higher values indicate greater carcinogenicity liability for long-term oral administration.
attribute.name: Predicted carcinogenicity probability
attribute.rationale: Long-term administration may elevate cancer risk; the carcinogenicity model (AUROC 0.7723) provides a computable surrogate. Retained as a preference, not an exclusion, because it is a predicted value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted carcinogenicity higher, favouring agents safer for long-term oral dosing.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted carcinogenicity probability does not correlate with observed carcinogenicity for kinase inhibitors, the criterion adds no value.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted acute toxicity as log(1/(mol/kg)) (LD50_Zhu endpoint); higher values indicate greater acute toxicity (smaller LD50).
attribute.name: Predicted acute toxicity LD50
attribute.rationale: Acute toxicity is a general safety concern; the LD50 model (R2 0.5959) provides a computable surrogate. Retained as a preference, not an exclusion, because it is a predicted value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted acute toxicity higher, favouring agents with a wider safety margin.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted LD50 does not correlate with observed acute toxicity for kinase inhibitors, the criterion is uninformative.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of skin reactions (Skin_Reaction endpoint); higher values indicate greater skin toxicity liability, a common adverse effect of kinase inhibitors.
attribute.name: Predicted skin reaction probability
attribute.rationale: Skin toxicity is the most frequent adverse effect of kinase inhibitors; the skin reaction model (AUROC 0.718) provides a computable surrogate. Retained as a preference, not an exclusion, because it is a predicted value.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted skin reaction probability higher, improving tolerability for chronic oral dosing.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted skin reaction probability does not correlate with observed skin toxicity for kinase inhibitors, the criterion adds no value.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound blocks the hERG potassium channel, an auxiliary cardiac-safety consideration for chronic oral dosing.
attribute.name: Predicted hERG blocking probability
attribute.rationale: Cardiac liability (QT prolongation, arrhythmias) is described in the claims as a concern for kinase-directed therapy. The hERG model is a computable auxiliary surrogate available for every compound with a structure; it is a preference, not a requirement, because no cited claim establishes hERG blockade as the operative mechanism or states a numeric threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted hERG blockade above those with higher probability, as an auxiliary cardiac-safety preference.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted hERG probability does not track the cardiac liability described in the claims, the preference adds no value.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound causes drug-induced liver injury, an auxiliary hepatic-safety consideration for chronic oral therapy.
attribute.name: Predicted drug-induced liver injury (DILI) probability
attribute.rationale: Hepatic adverse events (elevated transaminases, hypertransaminasemia) are reported in the claims. The DILI model is a computable auxiliary surrogate for every compound with a structure; it is a preference, not a requirement, because no cited claim establishes DILI probability as the operative liability or states a numeric threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted DILI probability above those with higher probability, as an auxiliary hepatic-safety preference.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted DILI probability does not track the hepatic adverse events described in the claims, the preference adds no value.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted probability of clinical trial toxicity or failure due to toxicity, an auxiliary general-safety consideration for chronic oral dosing.
attribute.name: Predicted clinical toxicity probability (ClinTox)
attribute.rationale: The claims describe severe toxicity and treatment discontinuation. ClinTox is a computable auxiliary broad toxicity liability score for every compound with a structure; it is a preference, not a requirement, because no cited claim establishes ClinTox probability as the operative liability or states a numeric threshold.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted clinical toxicity above those with higher probability, as an auxiliary general-safety preference.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted ClinTox probability does not track the toxicity/discontinuation rates described in the claims, the preference adds no value.

attribute.definition: Median curated pChEMBL value (pChEMBL = -log10 molar IC50/Ki/Kd/EC50) for the compound against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844), pooled from ChEMBL curated activity records and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology affinity records; higher pChEMBL indicates stronger CSF1R engagement.
attribute.name: CSF1R curated potency (pChEMBL, pooled ChEMBL + IUPHAR)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by pooled curated CSF1R potency; compounds with higher median pChEMBL rise above those with lower or absent curated CSF1R potency.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with no curated CSF1R pChEMBL record is later shown to engage CSF1R functionally at clinically relevant concentrations, this quantity's standing as the CSF1R engagement measure for screening is falsified.

attribute.definition: Median curated pChEMBL value (pChEMBL = -log10 molar IC50/Ki/Kd/EC50) for the compound against VEGFR1 (CHEMBL1868), pooled from ChEMBL curated activity records and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology affinity records; higher pChEMBL indicates stronger VEGFR1 engagement.
attribute.name: VEGFR1 curated potency (pChEMBL, pooled ChEMBL + IUPHAR)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by pooled curated VEGFR1 potency; compounds with higher median pChEMBL rise above those with lower or absent curated VEGFR1 potency.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with no curated VEGFR1 pChEMBL record is later shown to engage VEGFR1 functionally at clinically relevant concentrations, this quantity's standing as the VEGFR1 engagement measure for screening is falsified.

attribute.definition: Median curated pChEMBL value (pChEMBL = -log10 molar IC50/Ki/Kd/EC50) for the compound against VEGFR2 (CHEMBL279), pooled from ChEMBL curated activity records and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology affinity records; higher pChEMBL indicates stronger VEGFR2 engagement.
attribute.name: VEGFR2 curated potency (pChEMBL, pooled ChEMBL + IUPHAR)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by pooled curated VEGFR2 potency; compounds with higher median pChEMBL rise above those with lower or absent curated VEGFR2 potency.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with no curated VEGFR2 pChEMBL record is later shown to engage VEGFR2 functionally at clinically relevant concentrations, this quantity's standing as the VEGFR2 engagement measure for screening is falsified.

attribute.definition: Median curated pChEMBL value (pChEMBL = -log10 molar IC50/Ki/Kd/EC50) for the compound against VEGFR3 (CHEMBL1955), pooled from ChEMBL curated activity records and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology affinity records; higher pChEMBL indicates stronger VEGFR3 engagement.
attribute.name: VEGFR3 curated potency (pChEMBL, pooled ChEMBL + IUPHAR)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by pooled curated VEGFR3 potency; compounds with higher median pChEMBL rise above those with lower or absent curated VEGFR3 potency.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with no curated VEGFR3 pChEMBL record is later shown to engage VEGFR3 functionally at clinically relevant concentrations, this quantity's standing as the VEGFR3 engagement measure for screening is falsified.

attribute.definition: Median curated pChEMBL potency for the compound against FGFR1 (CHEMBL3650), pooled across ChEMBL and IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology curated measurements; higher pChEMBL indicates stronger FGFR1 engagement.
attribute.name: FGFR1 curated pChEMBL potency

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates by measured FGFR1 potency pooled from both curated sources; higher median pChEMBL ranks better, and candidates with no curated FGFR1 potency remain unknown on this criterion.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate ranked high on pooled FGFR1 pChEMBL fails to inhibit FGFR1 signalling in a functional assay, or a candidate with no curated FGFR1 record is shown to engage FGFR1, the pooled potency ordering is falsified as a measure of FGFR1 engagement.

attribute.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; presence of a record indicates engagement on record, while absence is unknown rather than evidence of inactivity.
attribute.name: CSF1R mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a curated CSF1R mechanism record rank above those without; absence of a record gives unknown rather than failure.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate carrying a curated CSF1R mechanism record is later shown not to engage CSF1R in functional assays, or a candidate with no record is shown to engage CSF1R, the categorical preference would need to be revisited.

attribute.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against VEGFR1 (CHEMBL1868) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; presence of a record indicates engagement on record, while absence is unknown rather than evidence of inactivity.
attribute.name: VEGFR1 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a curated VEGFR1 mechanism record rank above those without; absence of a record gives unknown rather than failure.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate carrying a curated VEGFR1 mechanism record is later shown not to engage VEGFR1 in functional assays, or a candidate with no record is shown to engage VEGFR1, the categorical preference would need to be revisited.

attribute.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against VEGFR2 (CHEMBL279) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; presence of a record indicates engagement on record, while absence is unknown rather than evidence of inactivity.
attribute.name: VEGFR2 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a curated VEGFR2 mechanism record rank above those without; absence of a record gives unknown rather than failure.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate carrying a curated VEGFR2 mechanism record is later shown not to engage VEGFR2 in functional assays, or a candidate with no record is shown to engage VEGFR2, the categorical preference would need to be revisited.

attribute.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; a present record indicates documented target engagement, absence yields unknown and never a fail.
attribute.name: CSF1R mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates carrying a curated CSF1R mechanism record rank above those without one, but absence does not exclude them, and conflicting records are routed to human review.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with a ChEMBL CSF1R mechanism record is later shown not to engage CSF1R in a functional assay, the reliability of that record would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against VEGFR1 (CHEMBL1868) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; a present record indicates documented target engagement, absence yields unknown and never a fail.
attribute.name: VEGFR1 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates carrying a curated VEGFR1 mechanism record rank above those without one, but absence does not exclude them, and conflicting records are routed to human review.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with a ChEMBL VEGFR1 mechanism record is later shown not to engage VEGFR1 in a functional assay, the reliability of that record would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against VEGFR2 (CHEMBL279) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; a present record indicates documented target engagement, absence yields unknown and never a fail.
attribute.name: VEGFR2 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates carrying a curated VEGFR2 mechanism record rank above those without one, but absence does not exclude them, and conflicting records are routed to human review.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with a ChEMBL VEGFR2 mechanism record is later shown not to engage VEGFR2 in a functional assay, the reliability of that record would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against VEGFR3 (CHEMBL1955) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; a present record indicates documented target engagement, absence yields unknown and never a fail.
attribute.name: VEGFR3 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates carrying a curated VEGFR3 mechanism record rank above those without one, but absence does not exclude them, and conflicting records are routed to human review.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with a ChEMBL VEGFR3 mechanism record is later shown not to engage VEGFR3 in a functional assay, the reliability of that record would be falsified.

attribute.definition: Categorical record from ChEMBL's mechanism-of-action table indicating that the compound engages FGFR1 (CHEMBL3650), pooled across curated mechanism entries for that target.
attribute.name: FGFR1 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a curated FGFR1 mechanism record rank above those without one.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound carrying a curated FGFR1 mechanism record is later shown not to engage FGFR1 functionally, the record's value as a preference signal is falsified.

attribute.definition: Number of Lipinski rule-of-five violations (molecular weight > 500, logP > 5, hydrogen-bond donors > 5, hydrogen-bond acceptors > 10) computed from the compound structure; lower counts indicate better oral drug-likeness and absorption potential. Values pooled from the contributing sources are reduced by median.
attribute.name: Lipinski rule of 5 violation count

payload.expected_change: Compounds with fewer predicted Lipinski rule-of-five violations rank above those with more in every contributing source; compounds without a structure receive unknown and are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with more predicted Lipinski violations is shown to be orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the ordering is not informative.

attribute.definition: ADMET-AI Pgp_Broccatelli classifier output: predicted probability in [0,1] that the compound inhibits P-glycoprotein; higher values indicate greater predicted P-gp inhibition, which can alter absorption, distribution and drug-drug interaction liability. Values pooled from the contributing sources are reduced by max, so the least favourable prediction governs.
attribute.name: Predicted P-glycoprotein inhibition probability

payload.expected_change: Compounds with lower pooled predicted P-gp inhibition probability rank above those with higher values; a compound whose pooled probability exceeds 0.5 is down-ranked, and compounds without a structure receive unknown and are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with pooled predicted P-gp inhibition probability above 0.5 is shown to have adequate oral absorption with no clinically significant transporter-mediated interaction, the boundary and ordering are falsified.

attribute.definition: Number of rotatable bonds, computed from the structure. Lower values indicate reduced molecular flexibility, which is generally associated with improved passive diffusion and oral bioavailability.
attribute.name: Rotatable bond count

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with fewer rotatable bonds above those with more, favouring better passive diffusion and oral bioavailability.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high rotatable bond count (>10) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), or rotatable bond count shows no correlation with permeability or oral bioavailability, the preference for fewer rotatable bonds is weakened.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound is absorbed from the human gastrointestinal tract, from the ADMET-AI HIA_Hou classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher values indicate better predicted intestinal absorption.
attribute.name: Predicted human intestinal absorption probability (HIA_Hou)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with predicted HIA_Hou probability at or above 0.5 above those below it, favouring intestinal absorption adequate for oral dosing.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted HIA_Hou does not correlate with measured absorption, or a compound with predicted probability <0.5 is shown to have adequate oral absorption in humans, the preference and its 0.5 model boundary are falsified.

attribute.definition: Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the ADMET-AI Bioavailability_Ma classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher values indicate better predicted oral exposure.
attribute.name: Predicted oral bioavailability probability (Bioavailability_Ma)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with predicted oral bioavailability probability at or above 0.5 above those below it, favouring oral exposure adequate for clinical development.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted oral bioavailability probability does not correlate with measured F%, or compounds below the 0.5 boundary show measured oral bioavailability comparable to those above it, the criterion's utility and its boundary are falsified.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model; higher values indicate greater solubility and lower risk of dissolution- or absorption-limited exposure.
attribute.name: Predicted aqueous solubility (log mol/L)

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with higher predicted aqueous solubility above those with lower solubility, favouring dissolution, absorption and oral exposure.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted aqueous solubility does not correlate with measured solubility, or compounds with low predicted solubility (e.g. below -4 log(mol/L)) show adequate oral absorption in humans, the preference is weakened.

attribute.definition: Model-predicted apparent permeability coefficient across Caco-2 monolayers from the ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang endpoint, in log(10^-6 cm/s). Higher values indicate greater intestinal permeability and a lower risk of absorption-limited oral exposure, so it is used as a ranking preference rather than an exclusion.
attribute.name: Predicted Caco-2 permeability (ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang, log 10^-6 cm/s)

attribute.definition: Fraction of an orally administered dose reaching the systemic circulation unchanged, measured in humans and expressed as percent, pooled across independent human clinical or PK studies; animal-only values are not eligible. The value is the median of the family's measurements.

interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are kinase inhibitors intended for oral administration, the same population the reported range describes, so treating the 500 Da edge as the preference line is a defensible transfer of the heuristic.

attribute.definition: Whether the compound is documented as orally administered in humans (e.g., approved oral drug, clinical trial oral dosing). This is a preference, not a requirement: absence of documentation gives unknown, never fail, because the oral route may simply be undocumented.
