bound_support.applicability_rationale: The passage reports that clinically relevant kinase inhibitors typically fall within approximately 380-500 Da and calls 500 Da close to the upper limit compatible with efficient passive diffusion; the candidate library consists of kinase inhibitors being screened for oral suitability, so the same upper edge applies.

interpretation.measurement: A reported typical range of approximately 380-500 Da for clinically relevant kinase inhibitors, with 500 Da described as close to the upper limit compatible with efficient passive diffusion.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are kinase inhibitors intended for oral administration, the same population the reported range describes, so treating the 500 Da edge as the preference line is a defensible transfer of the heuristic.

attribute.definition: Topological polar surface area in Å² computed from the compound's structure by the PubChem computed-descriptor route (derived, not a trained prediction). Lower values are associated with enhanced passive diffusion, and values at or below approximately 90 Å² lie in the low-polarity band the cited source links to improved penetration; the criterion is applied as a preference favouring oral absorption. Where a compound carries values from more than one source record, the pooled value is the median across them.
attribute.name: Topological polar surface area (TPSA)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates whose computed TPSA falls at or below 90 Å² above those with higher TPSA, so compounds with the polarity band associated with better passive diffusion and oral absorption are preferred; higher values are deprioritized, not excluded.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with computed TPSA above 90 Å² are found to have high measured human oral bioavailability (e.g. F% > 50%), the preference for lower TPSA would be weakened.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The source offers TPSA below approximately 90 Å² as the line correlating with improved passive diffusion and CNS penetration; the candidates are small-molecule kinase inhibitors being screened for oral absorption, the same chemical class the heuristic addresses. The heuristic is used as a preference line, not a hard exclusion.

interpretation.measurement: TPSA values below approximately 90 Å² correlate with improved CNS penetration
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are small-molecule kinase inhibitors being screened for oral absorption, the same class the heuristic addresses.

payload.definition: Presence of a curated mechanism-of-action record in ChEMBL stating that the compound engages VEGFR3 (CHEMBL1955); categorical engagement on record. The cited claims assert VEGFR3 engagement qualitatively; the categorical record is retrieved from the curated mechanism_records evidence lookup.
payload.name: VEGFR3 mechanism engagement (curated record)
payload.rationale: VEGFR3 is a required target; a curated mechanism record is independent evidence of engagement, covering compounds that may lack pChEMBL data. It is not a potency measure. The cited claims support VEGFR3 as a required target and assert engagement, but do not themselves provide a curated mechanism record; the attribute is populated from the curated mechanism_records evidence lookup. This attribute is one of five target-specific mechanism engagement attributes that together cover the concurrent five-target requirement.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with a curated VEGFR3 engagement record above those without; absence gives unknown, not failure.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with a curated VEGFR3 record is later shown not to engage VEGFR3 in functional assays, the preference would need to be revisited.

payload.definition: Reported absolute or relative oral bioavailability (F%) in humans, as a measured pharmacokinetic parameter. Higher values indicate greater fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation intact. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "oral bioavailability"

payload.name: Oral bioavailability (human, measured F%)
payload.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of an oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans. The objective requires oral administration; a measured human F% is a decision-relevant absorption parameter. Multiple claims report human F% values (e.g., 58%, 38-49%, 85-90%, 21.4%, 4.7%, 69-83%, 25%). No claim states a required minimum F%, so the rule ranks by value without a cutoff. The ordering is a preference, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower values.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with low measured F% is approved and clinically effective as an oral agent for the required targets, the preference ordering is challenged.

payload.definition: Median of reported times to maximum plasma concentration after oral administration, in hours; when a source reports only a range, the range midpoint is used. Lower values indicate faster absorption. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: longer Tmax may still be compatible with oral bioavailability and efficacy.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND "Tmax"

payload.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax, median of reported values)
payload.rationale: Tmax is a direct measure of oral absorption rate. Cited claims report measured Tmax values of 4 h and 3 h and ranges of 1-4 h, 2-4 h, 3-4 h and 6-12 h for orally administered agents, establishing the quantity as measurable and decision-relevant, but no claim states a required Tmax, so the rule ranks by value without a cutoff. The ordering is a preference, not a requirement: longer Tmax may still be compatible with oral bioavailability and efficacy.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with shorter Tmax above those with longer Tmax, without a numeric cutoff.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with longer Tmax is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the ordering is not informative.

payload.definition: Whether the compound is documented as orally administered in humans (e.g., approved oral drug, clinical trial oral dosing). This is a preference, not a requirement: absence of documentation gives unknown, never fail, because the oral route may simply be undocumented.
payload.name: Oral administration route (recorded)
payload.rationale: The task requires oral administration. This attribute records whether the compound has a documented oral route in humans. The route flag is a boolean; absence before approval gives unknown, never fail. Because the record flag is often empty for candidates whose oral route is simply undocumented, this is a preference rather than a hard exclusion: candidates with oral=true rank above those with unknown, and unknown is not penalized as a failure. Undocumented oral route compounds may still be orally bioavailable and effective.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with oral=true above those with unknown; candidates without a documented oral route are not excluded but are deprioritized.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate without a documented oral route is later found to be orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the preference for documented oral administration would be weakened.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The source offers logP ≈ 2–4 as the optimal range for kinase inhibitors; the lower edge is the heuristic line below which lipophilicity is suboptimal for passive diffusion.

interpretation.measurement: logP ≈ 2–4 is considered optimal for kinase inhibitors
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are kinase inhibitors being screened for oral developability, the same class the heuristic addresses.

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The source offers logP ≈ 2–4 as the optimal range for kinase inhibitors; the upper edge is the heuristic line above which lipophilicity compromises solubility and increases clearance.

interpretation.measurement: logP ≈ 2–4 is considered optimal for kinase inhibitors
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are kinase inhibitors being screened for oral developability, the same class the heuristic addresses.

payload.definition: Computed XLogP (log units) from PubChem. The source states moderate lipophilicity (logP ≈ 2–4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors; candidates are ranked by distance outside this band, with values inside the band scoring best.
payload.name: Lipophilicity (logP) within optimal kinase-inhibitor range
payload.rationale: Moderate lipophilicity (logP ≈ 2–4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors (claim_01M4YGKFT8T97H08A3RS5A2H24); excessive lipophilicity causes poor solubility and increased metabolic clearance (claim_01M4YGKFTX7A37M77HHQX99A1P). The range is a heuristic, so this is a preference ranking by distance outside the band, not a hard exclusion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with logP closer to the 2–4 range above those outside it, favouring compounds with optimal lipophilicity for oral absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with logP outside 2–4 are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), the preference for the 2–4 range would be weakened.

payload.definition: Fold-change in AUC due to food effect on oral absorption, as reported in clinical pharmacology studies or labels. A value of 1 indicates no food effect; values greater than 1 indicate increased exposure with food.

parameters.query_template: ({names}) AND ("food effect" OR "fasted" OR "fed") AND (pharmacokinetics OR absorption)

payload.name: Food effect on AUC (fold-change)
payload.rationale: Food effects can significantly alter oral exposure and complicate dosing. A smaller fold-change (closer to 1) is preferred for clinical development. The cited claims report food effects for specific agents, but no universal cutoff is stated, so this remains an exploratory consideration.

payload.expected_change: Candidates with smaller food-effect fold-changes are noted as more favorable.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with a significant food effect can be managed with dietary instructions without compromising efficacy, the consideration would be less important.

payload.definition: Model-predicted probability of blood-brain barrier penetration; lower probability is generally preferred for peripheral targets to minimise CNS side effects.
payload.name: Predicted blood-brain barrier penetration probability (BBB_Martins)
payload.rationale: BBB penetration can lead to CNS side effects; for oncology targets outside the CNS, lower penetration is often preferred. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.9004, supporting its use as a preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with lower predicted BBB penetration higher.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted BBB penetration does not correlate with measured brain penetration, the ranking value is reduced.

payload.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP2C9, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.
payload.name: Predicted CYP2C9 inhibition probability
payload.rationale: CYP2C9 inhibition is a common source of drug-drug interactions. The ADMET-AI CYP2C9_Veith endpoint provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.9077, supporting a preference rule.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted CYP2C9 inhibition probability higher.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted CYP2C9 inhibition probabilities do not correlate with measured CYP2C9 inhibition for a reference set, the attribute should be discarded.

payload.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP1A2, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.
payload.name: Predicted CYP1A2 inhibition probability
payload.rationale: CYP1A2 inhibition can alter the metabolism of co-administered drugs. The ADMET-AI CYP1A2_Veith endpoint provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.9411, supporting a preference rule.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted CYP1A2 inhibition probability higher.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted CYP1A2 inhibition probabilities do not correlate with measured CYP1A2 inhibition for a reference set, the attribute should be discarded.

payload.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP2C19, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.
payload.name: Predicted CYP2C19 inhibition probability
payload.rationale: CYP2C19 inhibition can alter the metabolism of co-administered drugs. The ADMET-AI CYP2C19_Veith endpoint provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.9062, supporting a preference rule.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted CYP2C19 inhibition probability higher.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted CYP2C19 inhibition probabilities do not correlate with measured CYP2C19 inhibition for a reference set, the attribute should be discarded.

payload.definition: Model-predicted probability that the compound is a CYP2C9 substrate, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater susceptibility to CYP2C9-mediated metabolism and potential drug-drug interactions.
payload.name: Predicted CYP2C9 substrate probability
payload.rationale: Being a CYP2C9 substrate increases the risk of metabolic drug-drug interactions. The ADMET-AI CYP2C9_Substrate_CarbonMangels endpoint provides a predicted probability for every compound with a structure. The model's held-out AUROC is 0.6279, so this is an auxiliary preference.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted CYP2C9 substrate probability higher.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted CYP2C9 substrate probabilities do not correlate with measured substrate status for a reference set, the attribute should be discarded.

payload.definition: Number of PAINS alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of assay interference and poor drug-likeness.
payload.name: Predicted PAINS alert count
payload.rationale: PAINS alerts flag compounds prone to assay interference, which can undermine development. The ADMET-AI PAINS_alert endpoint provides a count for every compound with a structure. This is a deterministic RDKit calculation, so it is reliable.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer PAINS alerts higher.
payload.falsification_test: If PAINS alert counts do not correlate with assay interference for a reference set, the attribute should be discarded.

payload.definition: Number of BRENK alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of problematic substructures.
payload.name: Predicted BRENK alert count
payload.rationale: BRENK alerts flag substructures associated with toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics. The ADMET-AI BRENK_alert endpoint provides a count for every compound with a structure. This is a deterministic RDKit calculation.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer BRENK alerts higher.
payload.falsification_test: If BRENK alert counts do not correlate with toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics for a reference set, the attribute should be discarded.

payload.definition: Number of NIH alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of problematic substructures.
payload.name: Predicted NIH alert count
payload.rationale: NIH alerts flag substructures associated with toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics. The ADMET-AI NIH_alert endpoint provides a count for every compound with a structure. This is a deterministic RDKit calculation.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with fewer NIH alerts higher.
payload.falsification_test: If NIH alert counts do not correlate with toxicity or poor pharmacokinetics for a reference set, the attribute should be discarded.

payload.definition: Model-predicted lipophilicity (logP) from the ADMET-AI Lipophilicity_AstraZeneca regression endpoint, in log units. The cited heuristic states that moderate lipophilicity (typically logP approximately 2-4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors, facilitating passive membrane diffusion without excessively compromising aqueous solubility. Candidates within this range rank higher than those outside it.
payload.name: Predicted lipophilicity
payload.rationale: The cited claim offers a heuristic that moderate lipophilicity (logP approximately 2-4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors, establishing lipophilicity as a relevant property. No cited claim states a decision threshold, so the rule ranks candidates by proximity to the cited optimal range rather than applying a cutoff. The range is recorded as context, not as a hard cutoff.

dissent.finding: The single cited claim asserts a heuristic that moderate logP (approximately 2-4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors, but the proposal's rule has cutoff null and cutoff_basis 'none_evidence_insufficient' while the definition states candidates within 2-4 rank higher. The heuristic is asserted, not validated for this library, and no measured or predicted logP values are cited to support applying it as a ranking criterion.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds within the cited optimal logP range (approximately 2-4) higher than those outside it.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds outside the 2-4 logP range show no difference in oral bioavailability or toxicity for kinase inhibitors, the criterion's utility is falsified.

payload.definition: Model-predicted volume of distribution (L/kg); affects tissue distribution and potential for toxicity.
payload.name: Predicted volume of distribution at steady state
payload.rationale: Volume of distribution influences tissue exposure and toxicity. The VDss_Lombardo model has negative R2 (-1.2107), meaning it does not beat the mean; therefore, this attribute is exploratory only and should not carry a cutoff.

payload.expected_change: Preserves predicted volume of distribution as a consideration without ranking, due to poor model performance.
payload.falsification_test: If the model's predictions show no correlation with observed volumes of distribution, its consideration value is falsified.

payload.definition: Model-predicted logP (RDKit); lower values are preferred because lipophilic, poorly soluble agents show food-dependent and variable oral absorption.
payload.name: Predicted logP (RDKit)
payload.rationale: The cited claim reports that lipophilic, poorly soluble agents have food-dependent absorption, supporting lower lipophilicity as a preference for consistent oral exposure. No cutoff is asserted because the claim states no logP number.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower predicted logP higher, favoring more consistent oral absorption.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with low predicted logP still show food-dependent or variable absorption, the rule's utility is falsified.

payload.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against CSF1R (CHEMBL1844) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; presence of a record indicates engagement on record, while absence is unknown rather than evidence of inactivity.
payload.name: CSF1R mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a curated CSF1R mechanism record rank above those without; absence of a record gives unknown rather than failure.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate carrying a curated CSF1R mechanism record is later shown not to engage CSF1R in functional assays, or a candidate with no record is shown to engage CSF1R, the categorical preference would need to be revisited.

payload.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against VEGFR1 (CHEMBL1868) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; presence of a record indicates engagement on record, while absence is unknown rather than evidence of inactivity.
payload.name: VEGFR1 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a curated VEGFR1 mechanism record rank above those without; absence of a record gives unknown rather than failure.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate carrying a curated VEGFR1 mechanism record is later shown not to engage VEGFR1 in functional assays, or a candidate with no record is shown to engage VEGFR1, the categorical preference would need to be revisited.

payload.definition: Categorical record of curated mechanism-of-action engagement against VEGFR2 (CHEMBL279) in ChEMBL's mechanism table; presence of a record indicates engagement on record, while absence is unknown rather than evidence of inactivity.
payload.name: VEGFR2 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a curated VEGFR2 mechanism record rank above those without; absence of a record gives unknown rather than failure.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate carrying a curated VEGFR2 mechanism record is later shown not to engage VEGFR2 in functional assays, or a candidate with no record is shown to engage VEGFR2, the categorical preference would need to be revisited.

payload.definition: Categorical record from ChEMBL's mechanism-of-action table indicating that the compound engages FGFR1 (CHEMBL3650), pooled across curated mechanism entries for that target.
payload.name: FGFR1 mechanism engagement

payload.expected_change: Candidates with a curated FGFR1 mechanism record rank above those without one.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound carrying a curated FGFR1 mechanism record is later shown not to engage FGFR1 functionally, the record's value as a preference signal is falsified.

payload.definition: Number of Lipinski rule-of-five violations (molecular weight > 500, logP > 5, hydrogen-bond donors > 5, hydrogen-bond acceptors > 10) computed from the compound structure; lower counts indicate better oral drug-likeness and absorption potential. Values pooled from the contributing sources are reduced by median.
payload.name: Lipinski rule of 5 violation count

payload.expected_change: Compounds with fewer predicted Lipinski rule-of-five violations rank above those with more in every contributing source; compounds without a structure receive unknown and are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a candidate with more predicted Lipinski violations is shown to be orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the ordering is not informative.

payload.definition: ADMET-AI Pgp_Broccatelli classifier output: predicted probability in [0,1] that the compound inhibits P-glycoprotein; higher values indicate greater predicted P-gp inhibition, which can alter absorption, distribution and drug-drug interaction liability. Values pooled from the contributing sources are reduced by max, so the least favourable prediction governs.
payload.name: Predicted P-glycoprotein inhibition probability

payload.expected_change: Compounds with lower pooled predicted P-gp inhibition probability rank above those with higher values; a compound whose pooled probability exceeds 0.5 is down-ranked, and compounds without a structure receive unknown and are not penalized.
payload.falsification_test: If a compound with pooled predicted P-gp inhibition probability above 0.5 is shown to have adequate oral absorption with no clinically significant transporter-mediated interaction, the boundary and ordering are falsified.

payload.definition: Number of rotatable bonds, computed from the structure. Lower values indicate reduced molecular flexibility, which is generally associated with improved passive diffusion and oral bioavailability.
payload.name: Rotatable bond count

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with fewer rotatable bonds above those with more, favouring better passive diffusion and oral bioavailability.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with high rotatable bond count (>10) are found to have high measured human F% (>50%), or rotatable bond count shows no correlation with permeability or oral bioavailability, the preference for fewer rotatable bonds is weakened.

payload.definition: Predicted probability that a compound is absorbed from the human gastrointestinal tract, from the ADMET-AI HIA_Hou classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher values indicate better predicted intestinal absorption.
payload.name: Predicted human intestinal absorption probability (HIA_Hou)

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates with predicted HIA_Hou probability at or above 0.5 above those below it, favouring intestinal absorption adequate for oral dosing.
payload.falsification_test: If predicted HIA_Hou does not correlate with measured absorption, or a compound with predicted probability <0.5 is shown to have adequate oral absorption in humans, the preference and its 0.5 model boundary are falsified.

payload.definition: Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the ADMET-AI Bioavailability_Ma classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher values indicate better predicted oral exposure.
payload.name: Predicted oral bioavailability probability (Bioavailability_Ma)

dissent.finding: The cited claims report measured oral bioavailability values and general determinants of oral absorption, but none validates the ADMET-AI Bioavailability_Ma classifier or its output scale for this library. The proposal's own falsification_test references a 0.5 boundary, yet the rule has cutoff null and cutoff_basis 'none_evidence_insufficient', so the boundary is not supported by cited evidence.

payload.falsification_test: If predicted oral bioavailability probability does not correlate with measured F%, or compounds below the 0.5 boundary show measured oral bioavailability comparable to those above it, the criterion's utility and its boundary are falsified.

payload.definition: Model-predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model; recorded as a descriptive consideration because the cited claims report solubility as a generic drug-like property and give low-solubility examples, without validating this endpoint or establishing a direction for this library.
payload.name: Predicted aqueous solubility (log mol/L)

payload.falsification_test: If predicted aqueous solubility does not correlate with measured solubility, or compounds with low predicted solubility show adequate oral absorption in humans, the consideration is weakened.

payload.definition: Model-predicted apparent permeability coefficient across Caco-2 monolayers from the ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang endpoint, in log(10^-6 cm/s); recorded as a descriptive consideration because the cited claims report low permeability for specific poorly absorbed compounds without validating this endpoint or establishing a direction for this library.

payload.definition: Molecular weight of the compound in Daltons (g/mol), computed from structure by the curated descriptor route rather than a trained prediction; lower values are preferred because size above roughly 500 Da approaches the upper limit compatible with efficient passive intestinal diffusion and increases efflux-transporter recognition.
payload.name: Molecular weight (Da)

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The passage reports that clinically relevant kinase inhibitors typically fall within approximately 380-500 Da and calls 500 Da close to the upper limit compatible with efficient passive diffusion; the candidate library consists of kinase inhibitors being screened for oral suitability, so the same upper edge applies.

interpretation.measurement: A reported typical range of approximately 380-500 Da for clinically relevant kinase inhibitors, with 500 Da described as close to the upper limit compatible with efficient passive diffusion.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are kinase inhibitors intended for oral administration, the same population the reported range describes, so treating the 500 Da edge as the preference line is a defensible transfer of the heuristic.

payload.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower computed molecular weight higher, placing compounds above the 500 g/mol heuristic below those at or under it, so that candidates whose size is compatible with efficient passive oral absorption come first.
payload.falsification_test: If molecular weight above 500 g/mol does not associate with reduced passive absorption or poorer oral exposure among kinase inhibitors in a reference set, the 500 g/mol bound and the ranking preference are falsified.

payload.definition: Topological polar surface area in Å² computed from the compound's structure by the PubChem computed-descriptor route (derived, not a trained prediction). Lower values are associated with enhanced passive diffusion, and values at or below approximately 90 Å² lie in the low-polarity band the cited source links to improved penetration; the criterion is applied as a preference favouring oral absorption. Where a compound carries values from more than one source record, the pooled value is the median across them.
payload.name: Topological polar surface area (TPSA)

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The source offers TPSA below approximately 90 Å² as the line correlating with improved passive diffusion and CNS penetration; the candidates are small-molecule kinase inhibitors being screened for oral absorption, the same chemical class the heuristic addresses. The heuristic is used as a preference line, not a hard exclusion.

interpretation.measurement: TPSA values below approximately 90 Å² correlate with improved CNS penetration
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are small-molecule kinase inhibitors being screened for oral absorption, the same class the heuristic addresses.

dissent.finding: The cited claim states that TPSA values below approximately 90 Å² correlate with improved CNS penetration, not with oral absorption or bioavailability. The proposal transfers this CNS-penetration heuristic to an oral-absorption preference line, which the cited claim does not support for this population.

payload.expected_change: Ranks candidates whose computed TPSA falls at or below 90 Å² above those with higher TPSA, so compounds with the polarity band associated with better passive diffusion and oral absorption are preferred; higher values are deprioritized, not excluded.
payload.falsification_test: If compounds with computed TPSA above 90 Å² are found to have high measured human oral bioavailability (e.g. F% > 50%), the preference for lower TPSA would be weakened.
